docs.title: Spectral Normative Modeling of Brain Structure
docs.text:
This repository provides the complete, reproducible analysis code accompanying the manuscript:

Mansour L., S., et al. (2026). Spectral Normative Modeling of Brain Structure. medRxiv. DOI: 10.1101/2025.01.16.25320639

The study introduces Spectral Normative Models (SNMs) — a framework for normative modeling of high-dimensional cortical phenotypes using spectral (eigenmode-based) representations. The repository contains every step of the analysis pipeline, from raw data preprocessing through model fitting, performance evaluation, and clinical application, enabling full reproduction of all manuscript figures and results.

docs.title: 🧰 SpectraNorm Package
docs.text:
The analysis code in this repository is built on top of SpectraNorm — a dedicated Python package we developed to facilitate the implementation of conventional and spectral normative models.

pip install spectranorm --upgrade

For tutorials, API reference, and further documentation, visit the SpectraNorm documentation site.

docs.title: 🔁 Reproducibility Walkthrough
docs.text: For a complete reproduction guide, including environment setup, runtime estimates, HPC requirements, and a figure-by-figure mapping from manuscript results to the notebook cells that produce them, see the provided Reproducibility Walkthrough.

docs.title: 📁 Repository Structure
docs.text: The analysis is organized into 9 sequential stages, each corresponding to a directory of Jupyter notebooks:

docs.title: 1. Data Import Scripts
docs.text:
Imports and preprocesses cortical thickness data from several large-scale neuroimaging datasets, comprising over 78,000 healthy brains from 30 different datasets. Includes:

  • Applying exclusion criteria to ensure data quality and consistency
  • Processing cortical thickness maps and transforming them to fs_LR 32k surface space
  • Preparing data for downstream analysis

docs.title: 2. Data Aggregation Scripts
docs.text:
Aggregates and prepares the cleaned data for normative modeling. Includes:

  • Combining cleaned data from multiple datasets
  • Final round of quality control
  • Random train/test split for model validation
  • Generating spectral coefficients of cortical thickness from vertex-wise data

docs.title: 3. Direct Normative Models
docs.text:
Specifies a direct normative modeling architecture as a backbone for the spectral model. Includes:

  • Implementing a Hierarchical Bayesian Regression normative model (via PyMC)
  • Fitting the model for a single variable (mean cortical thickness) as a function of age, sex, and site — used as a sanity check
  • This architecture is reused in subsequent notebooks for both direct and spectral implementations

docs.title: 4. Spectral Basis Construction
docs.text:
Generates the spectral basis functions (connectome eigenmodes) used to encode high-resolution cortical phenotypes. Includes:

  • Computing connectome-based brain eigenmodes via SVD of a random walk graph Laplacian shift operator

docs.title: 5. Spectral Normative Model Fitting
docs.text:
Fits the full Spectral Normative Model (SNM) using the spectral coefficients of cortical thickness. Includes:

  • Fitting the Spectral Normative Model (SNM)
  • Verifying the generation of normative ranges
  • Saving the fitted model for subsequent evaluation

docs.title: 6. Performance Evaluations
docs.text:
Evaluates SNM performance and benchmarks it against the direct normative model. Includes:

  • Evaluating accuracy across varying numbers of modes and spatial granularities
  • Comparing SNM and direct model performance
  • Reproducing comparative figures from the manuscript

docs.title: 7. Cortical Growth Gradients
docs.text:
Uses the fitted SNM to investigate cortical growth gradients across the lifespan. Includes:

  • Mapping three distinct cortical growth gradients
  • Comparing growth gradients to known cortical organization hierarchies
  • Characterizing lifespan trajectories of change

docs.title: 8. Clinical (AD) Evaluations
docs.text:
Applies the fitted SNM to a clinical Alzheimer's Disease (AD) sample. Includes:

  • Loading data from the MACC Harmonization dataset
  • Fine-tuning the healthy SNM via normative adaptation (site harmonization)
  • Mapping individual deviations from the normative model
  • Characterizing the normative signature of AD-related cortical atrophy
  • Assessing whether individual deviation patterns support discrete AD subtypes (clusterability analyses)

docs.title: 9. Data Sharing
docs.text:
Shares the data produced in this manuscript. Includes:

  • A pretrained SNM for cortical thickness
  • Normative brain charts for multiple cortical parcellations

🎨 Explore an interactive visualization of the pretrained SNM1000 vertex resolution charts

docs.title: 🗄️ Pretrained Model
docs.text:
The pretrained SNM1000 model is available as a release asset:

Download and decompress: 

wget https://github.com/sina-mansour/normative_brain_charts/releases/download/v1.0/pretrained_SNM_1000_V1.0.tar.gz
tar -xzvf pretrained_SNM_1000_V1.0.tar.gz

Load the model in Python: 

from spectranorm import snm

snm_1000 = snm.SpectralNormativeModel.load_model(
    "/<path-to-extracted-directory>/pretrained_SNM_1000_V1.0/"
)

For usage examples, refer to the notebooks on growth gradients, clinical application, and data sharing, as well as the SpectraNorm tutorials.

docs.title: Vertex-Wise Normative Charts
docs.text:
In addition to the parcellation-based charts, we also provide normative trajectories at the full vertex resolution of the fs_LR 32k surface mesh (~32,000 vertices per hemisphere).

Resolution Combined Female Male Vertex-wise (fs_LR 32k) 📄 📄 📄

These are stored as .joblib files and can be loaded directly into Python.

import joblib

# Load the normative trajectories
vertex_charts = joblib.load("/<path-to-file>/vertex-wise.fs_LR_32k.normative_trajectories.joblib")

docs.title: 🗺️ Cortical Maps
docs.text:
The cortical maps derived in this study are publicly available in the data/brainmaps/ directory. Each map is provided in both .dscalar.nii (CIFTI) and .npy (NumPy) formats.

The .dscalar.nii files can be visualized directly in Connectome Workbench, while the .npy files can be loaded in Python via numpy.load().

docs.title: Data Import
docs.text:
The training sample comprises 78,405 scans drawn from 30 datasets across 189 imaging sites. Each notebook below handles one data source: locating and downloading the imaging data where possible, applying the study's exclusion criteria, processing cortical thickness maps, and transforming them into fs_LR 32k surface space for downstream aggregation.

Datasets differ substantially in their access conditions. Some are openly available and are fetched programmatically within the notebook; others require approval from a data access committee or an executed data transfer agreement, in which case the notebook documents the processing applied to data obtained through those channels. No raw imaging data is redistributed through this repository.

docs.title: Reproducibility Walkthrough
docs.text:
This document provides a guide for reproducing the results reported in Mansour L. et al. (2026). Spectral Normative Modeling of Brain Structure. It is intended as the primary entry point for anyone wishing to verify, reproduce, or build on the manuscript's findings.

The walkthrough is organised into five sections:

  1. 🧰 Prerequisites: system tools and access requirements before installing the Python environment.
  2. 📦 Setting up the environment: installing dependencies and verifying the installation.
  3. ⏱️ Runtime expectations: approximate runtimes and hardware requirements for each part of the pipeline.
  4. 🖼️ Figure generation walkthrough: a figure-by-figure map linking each manuscript result to the notebook (and where possible, the specific cell) that produces it.
  5. 🛠️ If something doesn't work: common issues and where to find help.

Throughout this document, references to manuscript figures use the form Fig. N for main-text figures, Ext. Data Fig. E.N for extended data figures, and Fig. S.N for supplementary figures.

docs.title: System tools
docs.text:
In addition to the Python environment described in the next section, the following system tools must be installed.

LaTeX is required for figure rendering via matplotlib's text.usetex setting. The figures use Computer Modern fonts and standard scientific LaTeX packages.

  • Ubuntu/Debian: sudo apt install texlive-latex-extra texlive-fonts-recommended cm-super dvipng
  • macOS: Install MacTeX (full distribution), or BasicTeX followed by sudo tlmgr install cm-super type1cm dvipng standalone.
  • Windows: Install MiKTeX, which auto-installs missing packages on first use.

To verify the installation works with matplotlib:

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.rcParams['text.usetex'] = True
plt.figure(); plt.text(0.5, 0.5, r'$\alpha + \beta = \gamma$'); plt.show()

If this raises a RuntimeError mentioning latex or dvipng, the LaTeX installation is incomplete.

git-annex is required by datalad for fetching the public datasets provided by the Reproducible Brain Charts platform used in the early pipeline notebooks (stages 01–02). It is included as part of the conda environment described below, so most users do not need to install it separately. If you encounter issues with the conda-provided version, it can also be installed via the system package manager:

  • Ubuntu/Debian: sudo apt install git-annex
  • macOS: brew install git-annex
  • Windows: See the git-annex Windows installation guide.

docs.title: Data access
docs.text:
The manuscript integrates 30 publicly available neuroimaging datasets (see manuscript Section S.1.1, "Healthy Lifespan Imaging Data"), plus the MACC clinical cohort used in Sections 2.5–2.6. Each dataset is subject to its own access and usage agreements. While some datasets are openly available, others require approval through data access committees or the execution of material transfer or data-use agreements. Researchers interested in accessing these datasets should consult the corresponding data providers for specific access procedures.

Note that no raw imaging data is redistributed through this repository. Researchers wishing to re-execute the complete pipeline from scratch should obtain each dataset through its conventional access route. Where applicable, the figure-generating notebooks operate on outputs of the trained model, provided as part of the pretrained release, and can therefore be reproduced without access to the underlying imaging data. Reproducing the full training pipeline from raw data is supported but requires substantial compute resources (see Section 3).

Even for users who do not obtain the underlying data, the notebooks in this repository serve as a transparent record of the computational pipeline behind every manuscript figure. Each analysis step, from preprocessing through model fitting, evaluation, and figure generation, is documented in executable form alongside its corresponding outputs, allowing the methodology to be audited and adapted without rerunning the pipeline end-to-end.

docs.title: 2. 📦 Setting up the environment
docs.text:
Two environment files are provided at the repository root, serving different purposes.

environment.yml is all that most users will need. It lists the direct dependencies, pinned to the versions used to produce the manuscript, and is the recommended starting point on any platform:

conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate snm_env

Installation takes under five minutes on a typical laptop with a reasonable internet connection.

environment-full.yml is the complete record, for anyone who wants it: every package present in the environment used to produce the manuscript, transitive dependencies included, each pinned to an exact version. Build strings have been stripped from the export, so conda is free to select an appropriate build for the current platform. A small number of the pinned versions were resolved on Linux and may not have counterparts elsewhere, which is why environment.yml remains the recommended route for cross-platform installation.

docs.title: Verifying the installation
docs.text:
Once the environment is active, the following imports should all succeed:

import numpy, scipy, pandas, sklearn, matplotlib, seaborn
import nibabel, nilearn
import pymc, pytensor, arviz, xarray, h5py
import spectranorm, neuromaps, brainsmash
import Connectome_Spatial_Smoothing, cerebro
import gdist, trimesh, diptest, statsmodels
import joblib, tqdm, pyarrow, skimage
print('All critical imports succeeded')

docs.title: The R environment for SigClust2
docs.text: Nearly all analyses run in the Python environment described above. The one exception is the SigClust2 hierarchical significance test used in the AD clusterability analyses, which is implemented only as an R package and requires a small, separate conda environment. Setup instructions, the pinned package version, and the command to run the analysis are given in 📓 08_02_clinical_AD_cluster_analyses.ipynb cell 53.

docs.title: Downloading the pretrained model
docs.text:
The pretrained SNM-1000 model and derived normative charts are available as a release asset. To download:

wget https://github.com/sina-mansour/normative_brain_charts/releases/download/v1.0/pretrained_SNM_1000_V1.0.tar.gz
tar -xzvf pretrained_SNM_1000_V1.0.tar.gz

The extracted directory contains the model parameters needed by the figure-generating notebooks (Section 4).

docs.title: 3. ⏱️ Runtime expectations
docs.text:
The pipeline spans computational costs that vary by several orders of magnitude, from figure-generating notebooks that run in minutes to model fits that can take nearly a day. The table below gives approximate runtimes and indicates the hardware each stage realistically requires.

All timings were measured on a compute server with 64 vCPU cores and 251 GB of RAM, and are intended as general guidance rather than benchmarks. Actual runtimes will vary with hardware, parallelism, and parameter choices. Most steps used only a small fraction of the available memory; the notable exception is eigenmode extraction (stage 04), which is memory-intensive.

Hardware categories

Meaning 🔴 Requires a compute server, due to memory, storage, or parallelism demands 🟠 Benefits substantially from a server, but can be run on a single machine 🟢 Runs comfortably on a personal machine of the kind commonly used for neuroimaging research Stage Description Runtime Hardware 01 Data import and preprocessing (27 notebooks) 1–2 days 🔴 02 Data aggregation and spectral encoding 2–4 hours 🟠 03 Direct normative model (single phenotype) ~2 min 🟢 04 Connectome eigenmode construction ~12 h 🔴 05 Spectral normative model fit (k = 1000) ~8 h 🟠 05 Spectral normative model fit (k = 10 000) ~12 h 🔴 06 Systematic performance evaluations ~20 h 🔴 06 Publication figures ~20 min 🟢 07 Growth gradient analyses ~1 h 🟠 08 Clinical model fine-tuning ~11 h 🟠 08 Individual deviation mapping and analyses ~1 h 🟢 08 Supplementary video generation ~20 min 🟢 08 AD clusterability analyses ~40 min 🟢 09 Pretrained model and atlas charts ~2 min 🟢 09 Vertex-wise charts ~17 min 🟢

Stage 01. The figure above assumes preprocessed cortical thickness data is already available. It excludes the considerable time required to obtain data access approvals and to run FreeSurfer preprocessing, neither of which is performed within these notebooks.

Stage 05. Runtime scales with the number of retained eigenmodes and with model configuration. The 1000-mode model completes in less than a single working day and remains largely feasible on a personal machine, demonstrating the overall efficiency of the framework. The 10 000-mode model is substantially more demanding and should ideally be run on a capable compute server.

Stage 06. The bulk of the time is spent on systematic benchmarking across mode counts and spatial granularities, parallelised across cores. The publication figures are generated from cached outputs and their respective cells run comparably faster.

Stage 08. Only the transfer-learning step that adapts the pretrained model to the clinical site is computationally demanding; it accounts for approximately 11 of the stage's 13 hours. Everything downstream of that fit, including individual deviation mapping, figure generation, and the post-hoc analyses, runs considerably faster. The supplementary videos are generated by three encoding cells that a reader reproducing only the figures can skip.

Notebooks that operate on the pretrained model rather than retraining it (stages 06 figures, 07, 08 post-fit analyses, and 09) are tractable without a compute server. Reproducing the training pipeline end-to-end (stages 01–06) requires high-performance computing infrastructure.

docs.title: 4. 🖼️ Figure generation walkthrough
docs.text:
This section maps each manuscript figure to the notebook, and where possible the specific cell, that produces it. For each figure, the table provides:

  • 📓 Notebook: the source notebook in the repository.
  • 🖼️ Rendered view: a link to the output of the cell in the HTML rendering of that notebook, served via GitHub Pages. This allows each figure and the code that produced it to be inspected in a browser without local execution.
  • 🔗 Dependencies: upstream notebooks or cells whose outputs are required.
  • ⏱️ Runtime: approximate execution time for the cells listed under Rendered view.

Cells are referred to by the notebook they belong to, abbreviated by its numeric prefix. A reference to 07_01 cell 112, for example, points to the 112th cell of 📓 07_01_growth_gradients.ipynb, counting markdown and code cells together from the top.

Several manuscript figures are composites. The notebooks produce individual panels, and the final figure is assembled from those panels, in some cases within a later notebook cell and in others manually in Inkscape. Where a figure is assembled manually, the table links to the cells that produce its constituent panels and names the panel each corresponds to.

The Dependencies column lists the immediate upstream requirements only. Most of these have dependencies of their own, so a reader reproducing the pipeline from scratch should run the notebooks in numerical order and execute the cells within each notebook sequentially from top to bottom, rather than attempting to satisfy individual dependencies in isolation.

Runtimes are banded and refer only to the compute time of the cells listed under Rendered view, measured on the hardware described in Section 3. They exclude upstream dependencies, and they also exclude the iterative development and manual styling that preceded each final figure. Figure 1 illustrates the gap: its programmatically generated panel runs in seconds, while the two schematic panels beside it were assembled by hand over several hours.

docs.title: Environment installation
docs.text:
If conda env create reports a PackagesNotFoundError, the most likely explanation is that environment-full.yml was used on a platform other than Linux, and one of its exact pinned versions has no counterpart there. Use environment.yml, which is the cross-platform file.

If conda env create reports a LinkError mentioning git-annex or compiler tools, the conda-provided git-annex is failing to install. Either install git-annex separately via your system package manager and remove it from the environment file, or install the gxx_linux-64 package into your base conda environment to provide the required toolchain.

docs.title: Figures look different from the manuscript
docs.text:
If figures render but text appears in a sans-serif font rather than Computer Modern, LaTeX is not being used. Verify your LaTeX installation as described in Section 1.

If figures are missing or contain only axes with no data, the most likely cause is a missing intermediate file. Check the Dependencies column for the relevant figure in Section 4 and run the upstream notebooks first.

docs.title: Where to get help
docs.text:
For issues specific to this repository, open an issue at github.com/sina-mansour/normative_brain_charts/issues.

For questions about the underlying SNM framework, see the spectranorm documentation.

For correspondence about the manuscript itself, contact the corresponding authors as listed in the published paper.

class MyNumpyEncoder(json.JSONEncoder):
    def default(self, obj):
        if isinstance(obj, np.integer):
            return int(obj)
        elif isinstance(obj, np.floating):
            return float(obj)
        elif isinstance(obj, np.ndarray):
            return obj.tolist()
        else:
            return super(MyEncoder, self).default(obj)


def ensure_dir(file_name):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(file_name), exist_ok=True)
    return file_name


def list_dirs(path=os.getcwd()):
    files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, '*'))
    files = [x for x in files if os.path.isdir(x)]
    return files


def file_exists(file_name, path_name=os.getcwd()):
    return os.path.isfile(os.path.join(path_name, file_name))


def write_json(json_obj, file_path):
    with open(file_path, 'w') as outfile:
        json.dump(json_obj, outfile, sort_keys=True, indent=4,
                  cls=MyNumpyEncoder)
    return json_obj


def write_np(np_obj, file_path):

    def default(self, obj):
        if isinstance(obj, np.integer):
            return int(obj)
        elif isinstance(obj, np.floating):
            return float(obj)

def ensure_dir(file_name):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(file_name), exist_ok=True)
    return file_name


def list_dirs(path=os.getcwd()):
    files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, '*'))
    files = [x for x in files if os.path.isdir(x)]
    return files


def file_exists(file_name, path_name=os.getcwd()):
    return os.path.isfile(os.path.join(path_name, file_name))


def write_json(json_obj, file_path):
    with open(file_path, 'w') as outfile:
        json.dump(json_obj, outfile, sort_keys=True, indent=4,
                  cls=MyNumpyEncoder)
    return json_obj


def load_json(file_path):
    with open(file_path, 'r') as infile:
        return json.load(infile)


def write_np(np_obj, file_path):
    with open(file_path, 'wb') as outfile:
        np.save(outfile, np_obj)

Long story short:

The approach that does what I want is achieved by:

  • First install and configure globus connect personal (./globusconnectpersonal -setup)
  • Configure authentication via Lasso
  • Install globus cli and login (globus login)
  • Initiate the following transfer command
globus transfer \
    "41494652-d3e1-498d-b97a-5ecb65b323ed:/dairc/derivatives/freesurfer/" \
    "<destination_endpoint>:/mountpoint/data/Globus/data/ABCD/freesurfer/" \
    --recursive --label "ABCD freesurfer selective derivative transfer" \
    --include "lh.white" --include "rh.white" \
    --include "lh.pial" --include "rh.pial" \
    --include "lh.thickness" --include "rh.thickness" \
    --include "lh.orig.nofix" --include "rh.orig.nofix" \
    --include "lh.sphere.reg" --include "rh.sphere.reg" \
    --exclude "*" --verify-checksum --dry-run

def process_subject(idx, subject, dataset, dataset_path):
    sub_dir = f"{idx:02d}"[-2:]
    
    tar_path = dataset_path / f"freesurfer/sub-{subject}/sub-{subject}_freesurfer.tar.xz"
    freesurfer_directory = f"/mountpoint/data/RBC/snm_thickness/{dataset}/freesurfer/{subject}/"
    thickness_fslr_output = f"/mountpoint/data/normative/fs_LR_32k/{dataset}/{sub_dir}/{subject}.thickness.fslr.npy"

    if os.path.exists(thickness_fslr_output):
        return f"Skipping {subject}, already processed"

    if not tar_path.parent.exists():
        return f"Skipping {subject}, no TAR at {tar_path}"

    # Download
    dl.get(tar_path, dataset=dataset_path, result_renderer="disabled")

    # Extract needed files
    try:
        with tarfile.open(tar_path, mode="r:xz") as tar:
            for item in items:
                file_in_tar = f"sub-{subject}/surf/{item}"
                tar.extract(file_in_tar, path=freesurfer_directory)
    except tarfile.ReadError as e:
        return f"Skipping {subject}, corrupt TAR: {e}"

    # Drop the TAR
    dl.drop(tar_path, dataset=dataset_path, result_renderer="disabled")

    # Compute
    transformed_fslr_thickness = snm.utils.nitools.compute_fslr_thickness(
        os.path.join(freesurfer_directory, f"sub-{subject}")
    )
    np.save(
        ensure_dir(thickness_fslr_output),
        transformed_fslr_thickness.astype(np.float32)
    )

    # Cleanup
    shutil.rmtree(freesurfer_directory, ignore_errors=True)

    return f"Done {subject}"

def process_subject_session(idx, subject, session, dataset, dataset_path):
    sub_dir = f"{idx:02d}"[-2:]
    
    tar_path = dataset_path / f"freesurfer/sub-{subject}_ses-{session}/sub-{subject}_ses-{session}_freesurfer.tar.xz"
    freesurfer_directory = f"/mountpoint/data/RBC/snm_thickness/{dataset}/freesurfer/sub-{subject}_ses-{session}/"
    thickness_fslr_output = f"/mountpoint/data/normative/fs_LR_32k/{dataset}/{sub_dir}/{subject}-{session}.thickness.fslr.npy"

    if os.path.exists(thickness_fslr_output):
        return f"Skipping {subject}-{session}, already processed"

    if not tar_path.parent.exists():
        return f"Skipping {subject}-{session}, no TAR at {tar_path}"

    # Download
    dl.get(tar_path, dataset=dataset_path, result_renderer="disabled")

    # Extract needed files
    try:
        with tarfile.open(tar_path, mode="r:xz") as tar:
            for item in items:
                file_in_tar = f"sub-{subject}_ses-{session}/surf/{item}"
                tar.extract(file_in_tar, path=freesurfer_directory)
    except tarfile.ReadError as e:
        return f"Skipping {subject}-{session}, corrupt TAR: {e}"

    # Drop the TAR
    dl.drop(tar_path, dataset=dataset_path, result_renderer="disabled")

    # Compute
    transformed_fslr_thickness = snm.utils.nitools.compute_fslr_thickness(
        os.path.join(freesurfer_directory, f"sub-{subject}_ses-{session}")
    )
    np.save(
        ensure_dir(thickness_fslr_output),
        transformed_fslr_thickness.astype(np.float32)
    )

    # Cleanup
    shutil.rmtree(freesurfer_directory, ignore_errors=True)

    return f"Done {subject}-{session}"

def process_subject_session(idx, subject, session, dataset, dataset_path):
    sub_dir = f"{idx:02d}"[-2:]
    
    tar_path = dataset_path / f"freesurfer/sub-{subject}_ses-{session}/sub-{subject}_ses-{session}_freesurfer.tar.xz"
    freesurfer_directory = f"/mountpoint/data/RBC/snm_thickness/{dataset}/freesurfer/sub-{subject}_ses-{session}/"
    thickness_fslr_output = f"/mountpoint/data/normative/fs_LR_32k/{dataset}/{sub_dir}/{subject}-{session}.thickness.fslr.npy"

    if os.path.exists(thickness_fslr_output):
        return f"Skipping {subject}-{session}, already processed"

    if not tar_path.parent.exists():
        return f"Skipping {subject}-{session}, no TAR at {tar_path}"

    # Download
    dl.get(tar_path, dataset=dataset_path, result_renderer="disabled")

    # Extract needed files
    try:
        with tarfile.open(tar_path, mode="r:xz") as tar:
            # Get all members (file paths inside the tar)
            members = tar.getnames()
            # Grab the top-level directory (first component of the first member)
            topdir = members[0].split("/")[0]
            for item in items:
                # file_in_tar = f"sub-{subject}_ses-{session}/surf/{item}"
                file_in_tar = f"{topdir}/surf/{item}"
                tar.extract(file_in_tar, path=freesurfer_directory)
    except tarfile.ReadError as e:
        return f"Skipping {subject}-{session}, corrupt TAR: {e}"

    # Drop the TAR
    dl.drop(tar_path, dataset=dataset_path, result_renderer="disabled")

    # Compute
    transformed_fslr_thickness = snm.utils.nitools.compute_fslr_thickness(
        # os.path.join(freesurfer_directory, f"sub-{subject}_ses-{session}")
        os.path.join(freesurfer_directory, topdir)
    )
    np.save(
        ensure_dir(thickness_fslr_output),
        transformed_fslr_thickness.astype(np.float32)
    )

    # Cleanup
    shutil.rmtree(freesurfer_directory, ignore_errors=True)

    return f"Done {subject}-{session}"

import numpy as np

items = [
    "lh.white", "rh.white",
    "lh.pial", "rh.pial",
    "lh.thickness", "rh.thickness",
    "lh.orig.nofix", "rh.orig.nofix",
    "lh.sphere.reg", "rh.sphere.reg",
]

def process_subject(idx, subject, dataset):
    sub_dir = f"{idx:02d}"[-2:]
    
    sub_id = subject.split('_')[0][3:]
    ses_id = f"{int(subject.split('_')[1][3:]):02d}"
    
    sshfs_directory = f"/home/ubuntu/cambridgemount/BGSP/BIDS/derivatives/freesurfer/sub-{sub_id}/ses-{ses_id}/run-1/surfaces/sub-{sub_id}/"
    freesurfer_directory = f"/mountpoint/data/CSD3/snm_thickness/{dataset}/freesurfer/{subject}/"
    thickness_fslr_output = f"/mountpoint/data/normative/fs_LR_32k/{dataset}/{sub_dir}/{subject}.thickness.fslr.npy"
    euler_number_output = f"/mountpoint/data/normative/eno/{dataset}/{sub_dir}/{subject}.eno.npy"

    if os.path.exists(thickness_fslr_output):
        return f"Skipping {subject}, already processed"

    if not Path(sshfs_directory).exists():
        return f"Skipping {subject}, no sshfs directory at {sshfs_directory}"

    # Copy needed files
    for item in items:
        src_file = Path(sshfs_directory) / f"surf/{item}"
        dst_file = Path(freesurfer_directory) / f"surf/{item}"
        # Make sure source exists
        if src_file.exists():
            # Make sure destination exists
            dst_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            # Copy the file
            shutil.copy(src_file, dst_file)
        else:
            return f"Skipping {subject}, missing file: {src_file}"

    # Compute
    transformed_fslr_thickness = snm.utils.nitools.compute_fslr_thickness(freesurfer_directory)
    np.save(
        ensure_dir(thickness_fslr_output),
        transformed_fslr_thickness.astype(np.float32)
    )
    euler_number = snm.utils.nitools.compute_total_euler_number(freesurfer_directory)
    np.save(
        ensure_dir(euler_number_output),
        euler_number
    )

    # Cleanup
    shutil.rmtree(freesurfer_directory, ignore_errors=True)

    return f"Done {subject}"

import joblib
import tarfile, os, shutil
import numpy as np

items = [
    "lh.white", "rh.white",
    "lh.pial", "rh.pial",
    "lh.thickness", "rh.thickness",
    "lh.orig.nofix", "rh.orig.nofix",
    "lh.sphere.reg", "rh.sphere.reg",
]

def process_subject(idx, subject, dataset):
    sub_dir = f"{idx:02d}"[-2:]
    sub_id = f"{subject:07d}"
    
    sshfs_directory = f"/home/ubuntu/cambridgemount/DLBS/BIDS/derivatives/freesurfer/sub-{sub_id}/session_1/run-1/surfaces/sub-{sub_id}/"
    freesurfer_directory = f"/mountpoint/data/CSD3/snm_thickness/{dataset}/freesurfer/{subject}/"
    thickness_fslr_output = f"/mountpoint/data/normative/fs_LR_32k/{dataset}/{sub_dir}/{subject}.thickness.fslr.npy"
    euler_number_output = f"/mountpoint/data/normative/eno/{dataset}/{sub_dir}/{subject}.eno.npy"

    if os.path.exists(thickness_fslr_output):
        return f"Skipping {subject}, already processed"

    if not Path(sshfs_directory).exists():
        return f"Skipping {subject}, no sshfs directory at {sshfs_directory}"

    # Copy needed files
    for item in items:
        src_file = Path(sshfs_directory) / f"surf/{item}"
        dst_file = Path(freesurfer_directory) / f"surf/{item}"
        # Make sure source exists
        if src_file.exists():
            # Make sure destination exists
            dst_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            # Copy the file
            shutil.copy(src_file, dst_file)
        else:
            return f"Skipping {subject}, missing file: {src_file}"

    # Compute
    transformed_fslr_thickness = snm.utils.nitools.compute_fslr_thickness(freesurfer_directory)
    np.save(
        ensure_dir(thickness_fslr_output),
        transformed_fslr_thickness.astype(np.float32)
    )
    euler_number = snm.utils.nitools.compute_total_euler_number(freesurfer_directory)
    np.save(
        ensure_dir(euler_number_output),
        euler_number
    )

    # Cleanup
    shutil.rmtree(freesurfer_directory, ignore_errors=True)

    return f"Done {subject}"

import joblib

import numpy as np

items = [
    "lh.white", "rh.white",
    "lh.pial", "rh.pial",
    "lh.thickness", "rh.thickness",
    "lh.orig.nofix", "rh.orig.nofix",
    "lh.sphere.reg", "rh.sphere.reg",
]

def process_subject(idx, subject, dataset):
    sub_dir = f"{idx:02d}"[-2:]
    
    sshfs_directory = f"/home/ubuntu/cambridgemount/ADHD200/BIDS/derivatives/freesurfer/{subject}/ses-1/run-1/surfaces/{subject}/"
    freesurfer_directory = f"/mountpoint/data/CSD3/snm_thickness/{dataset}/freesurfer/{subject}/"
    thickness_fslr_output = f"/mountpoint/data/normative/fs_LR_32k/{dataset}/{sub_dir}/{subject}.thickness.fslr.npy"
    euler_number_output = f"/mountpoint/data/normative/eno/{dataset}/{sub_dir}/{subject}.eno.npy"

    if os.path.exists(thickness_fslr_output):
        return f"Skipping {subject}, already processed"

    if not Path(sshfs_directory).exists():
        return f"Skipping {subject}, no sshfs directory at {sshfs_directory}"

    # Copy needed files
    for item in items:
        src_file = Path(sshfs_directory) / f"surf/{item}"
        dst_file = Path(freesurfer_directory) / f"surf/{item}"
        # Make sure source exists
        if src_file.exists():
            # Make sure destination exists
            dst_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            # Copy the file
            shutil.copy(src_file, dst_file)
        else:
            return f"Skipping {subject}, missing file: {src_file}"

    # Compute
    transformed_fslr_thickness = snm.utils.nitools.compute_fslr_thickness(freesurfer_directory)
    np.save(
        ensure_dir(thickness_fslr_output),
        transformed_fslr_thickness.astype(np.float32)
    )
    euler_number = snm.utils.nitools.compute_total_euler_number(freesurfer_directory)
    np.save(
        ensure_dir(euler_number_output),
        euler_number
    )

    # Cleanup
    shutil.rmtree(freesurfer_directory, ignore_errors=True)

    return f"Done {subject}"

import joblib

import numpy as np

items = [
    "lh.white", "rh.white",
    "lh.pial", "rh.pial",
    "lh.thickness", "rh.thickness",
    "lh.orig.nofix", "rh.orig.nofix",
    "lh.sphere.reg", "rh.sphere.reg",
]

def process_subject(idx, subject, freesurfer_path, dataset):
    sub_dir = f"{idx:02d}"[-2:]
    
    sshfs_directory = freesurfer_path
    freesurfer_directory = f"/mountpoint/data/CSD3/snm_thickness/{dataset}/freesurfer/{subject}/"
    thickness_fslr_output = f"/mountpoint/data/normative/fs_LR_32k/{dataset}/{sub_dir}/{subject}.thickness.fslr.npy"
    euler_number_output = f"/mountpoint/data/normative/eno/{dataset}/{sub_dir}/{subject}.eno.npy"

    if os.path.exists(thickness_fslr_output):
        return f"Skipping {subject}, already processed"

    if not Path(sshfs_directory).exists():
        return f"Skipping {subject}, no sshfs directory at {sshfs_directory}"

    # Copy needed files
    for item in items:
        src_file = Path(sshfs_directory) / f"surf/{item}"
        dst_file = Path(freesurfer_directory) / f"surf/{item}"
        # Make sure source exists
        if src_file.exists():
            # Make sure destination exists
            dst_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            # Copy the file
            shutil.copy(src_file, dst_file)
        else:
            return f"Skipping {subject}, missing file: {src_file}"

    # Compute
    transformed_fslr_thickness = snm.utils.nitools.compute_fslr_thickness(freesurfer_directory)
    np.save(
        ensure_dir(thickness_fslr_output),
        transformed_fslr_thickness.astype(np.float32)
    )
    euler_number = snm.utils.nitools.compute_total_euler_number(freesurfer_directory)
    np.save(
        ensure_dir(euler_number_output),
        euler_number
    )

    # Cleanup
    shutil.rmtree(freesurfer_directory, ignore_errors=True)

    return f"Done {subject}"

        # Make sure source exists
        if src_file.exists():
            # Make sure destination exists
            dst_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            # Copy the file
            shutil.copy(src_file, dst_file)
        else:
            return f"Skipping {subject}, missing file: {src_file}"

    # Compute
    transformed_fslr_thickness = snm.utils.nitools.compute_fslr_thickness(freesurfer_directory)
    np.save(

    euler_number = snm.utils.nitools.compute_total_euler_number(freesurfer_directory)
    np.save(
        ensure_dir(euler_number_output),
        euler_number
    )

    # Cleanup
    shutil.rmtree(freesurfer_directory, ignore_errors=True)

    return f"Done {subject}"

import joblib

import numpy as np

items = [
    "lh.white", "rh.white",
    "lh.pial", "rh.pial",
    "lh.thickness", "rh.thickness",
    "lh.orig.nofix", "rh.orig.nofix",
    "lh.sphere.reg", "rh.sphere.reg",
]

def process_subject(idx, subject, dataset):
    sub_dir = f"{idx:02d}"[-2:]
    
    sshfs_directory = f"/home/ubuntu/asrbmount/T1/FS/{subject}/"
    freesurfer_directory = f"/mountpoint/data/CSD3/snm_thickness/{dataset}/freesurfer/{subject}/"
    thickness_fslr_output = f"/mountpoint/data/normative/fs_LR_32k/{dataset}/{sub_dir}/{subject}.thickness.fslr.npy"
    euler_number_output = f"/mountpoint/data/normative/eno/{dataset}/{sub_dir}/{subject}.eno.npy"

    if os.path.exists(thickness_fslr_output):
        return f"Skipping {subject}, already processed"

    if not Path(sshfs_directory).exists():
        return f"Skipping {subject}, no sshfs directory at {sshfs_directory}"

    # Copy needed files
    for item in items:
        src_file = Path(sshfs_directory) / f"surf/{item}"
        dst_file = Path(freesurfer_directory) / f"surf/{item}"
        # Make sure source exists
        if src_file.exists():
            # Make sure destination exists
            dst_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            # Copy the file
            shutil.copy(src_file, dst_file)
        else:
            return f"Skipping {subject}, missing file: {src_file}"

    # Compute
    transformed_fslr_thickness = snm.utils.nitools.compute_fslr_thickness(freesurfer_directory)
    np.save(
        ensure_dir(thickness_fslr_output),
        transformed_fslr_thickness.astype(np.float32)
    )
    euler_number = snm.utils.nitools.compute_total_euler_number(freesurfer_directory)
    np.save(
        ensure_dir(euler_number_output),
        euler_number
    )

    # Cleanup
    shutil.rmtree(freesurfer_directory, ignore_errors=True)

    return f"Done {subject}"

import joblib

import numpy as np

items = [
    "lh.white", "rh.white",
    "lh.pial", "rh.pial",
    "lh.thickness", "rh.thickness",
    "lh.orig.nofix", "rh.orig.nofix",
    "lh.sphere.reg", "rh.sphere.reg",
]

def process_subject(idx, subject, session, dataset):
    sub_dir = f"{idx:02d}"[-2:]
    
    sshfs_directory = f"/home/ubuntu/cambridgemount/WAYNE/BIDS/derivatives/freesurfer/{subject}/ses-Wave{session}/run-1/surfaces/{subject}/"
    freesurfer_directory = f"/mountpoint/data/CSD3/snm_thickness/{dataset}/freesurfer/{subject}-{session}/"
    # thickness_fslr_output = f"/mountpoint/data/normative/fs_LR_32k/{dataset}/{sub_dir}/{subject}.thickness.fslr.npy"
    thickness_fslr_output = f"/mountpoint/data/normative/fs_LR_32k/{dataset}/{sub_dir}/{subject}-{session}.thickness.fslr.npy"
    # euler_number_output = f"/mountpoint/data/normative/eno/{dataset}/{sub_dir}/{subject}.eno.npy"
    euler_number_output = f"/mountpoint/data/normative/eno/{dataset}/{sub_dir}/{subject}-{session}.eno.npy"

    if os.path.exists(thickness_fslr_output):
        return f"Skipping {subject}, already processed"

    if not Path(sshfs_directory).exists():
        return f"Skipping {subject}, no sshfs directory at {sshfs_directory}"

    # Copy needed files
    for item in items:
        src_file = Path(sshfs_directory) / f"surf/{item}"
        dst_file = Path(freesurfer_directory) / f"surf/{item}"
        # Make sure source exists
        if src_file.exists():
            # Make sure destination exists
            dst_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            # Copy the file
            shutil.copy(src_file, dst_file)
        else:
            return f"Skipping {subject}, missing file: {src_file}"

    # Compute
    transformed_fslr_thickness = snm.utils.nitools.compute_fslr_thickness(freesurfer_directory)
    np.save(
        ensure_dir(thickness_fslr_output),
        transformed_fslr_thickness.astype(np.float32)
    )
    euler_number = snm.utils.nitools.compute_total_euler_number(freesurfer_directory)
    np.save(
        ensure_dir(euler_number_output),
        euler_number
    )

    # Cleanup
    shutil.rmtree(freesurfer_directory, ignore_errors=True)

    return f"Done {subject}"

import os

def compute_spectral_coeffs(data_paths, output_path=None, eigenmode_basis=eigenmode_basis):
    coeffs = np.nan * np.zeros(
        (len(data_paths), eigenmode_basis.n_modes),
        dtype=eigenmode_basis.eigenvectors.dtype,
    )
    for i, data_path in enumerate(data_paths):
        coeffs[i, :] = np.load(data_path) @ eigenmode_basis.eigenvectors

    if output_path is not None:
        np.save(output_path, coeffs)

    return coeffs

This notebook utilizes the eigenmode basis (computed in 04_1) to map the spectral coefficients of high-resolution cortical thickness phenotypes for all individual scans passing inclusion criteria (excluding individuals with medical diagnosis, low quality surface reconstructions, as well as excluding repeat scans of the same individual).

These spectral coefficients will be used in later notebooks (e.g. 05_01) to fit SNM.

Note: This notebook should be executed after 04_01

# Let's write a function that automates the visualization of harmonized data along with the normative charts

def plot_charts(ax, data, harmonized_spectral_coeff_data, dummy_ages, predicted_moments, query_index):
    # extract predicted moments
    y_ppc_mu_mean = predicted_moments['mu_estimate'][:, query_index]
    y_ppc_sigma_mean = predicted_moments['std_estimate'][:, query_index]

    quantiles = [0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.95, 0.99, 0.999]

    thickness_quantiles = {
        q: (
            (
                y_ppc_mu_mean + stats.norm.ppf(q=q) * (y_ppc_sigma_mean)
            )
        ) for q in quantiles
    }

    # colors for the plot
    c1 = '#448e9c'  # brighter shade
    c2 = '#038da6'  # darker shade

    # centile plots
    for q1, q2, alpha in [(0.001, 0.999, 0.05), (0.01, 0.99, 0.1), (0.05, 0.95, 0.2), (0.25, 0.75, 0.3)]:
        ax.fill_between(
            dummy_ages,
            thickness_quantiles[q1],
            thickness_quantiles[q2],
            alpha=alpha,
            color=c1,
        )

        # Now add boundary lines with different colors
        ax.plot(dummy_ages, thickness_quantiles[q1], color=c1, lw=0.5, linestyle=":",)
        ax.plot(dummy_ages, thickness_quantiles[q2], color=c1, lw=0.5, linestyle=":",)

    # Median
    ax.plot(
        dummy_ages,
        thickness_quantiles[0.5],
        c=c2,
        lw=4,
    )

    ax.set_xlim(3.5,96.5)

    tmp_df = data.copy()
    tmp_df['harmonized_thickness'] = harmonized_spectral_coeff_data[:, query_index]

    sns.scatterplot(
        data=tmp_df,
        x='age',
        y='harmonized_thickness',
        ax=ax,
        linewidth=0,
        hue='sex',
        palette="colorblind",
        alpha = 0.5,
        s=10,
        zorder=-20,
    )

    # Move legend outside
    legend = ax.legend(
        bbox_to_anchor=(0.98, 0.98),    # x=1.05 pushes it outside the axes
        loc='upper right',            # anchor point for placement
        borderaxespad=-0.,            # padding
        fontsize=8,                 # font size
        markerscale=1,               # scale up legend markers (3x bigger than in the plot)
    )
    
    ax.set_ylabel(f"Mode: {query_index + 1}")

class MyNumpyEncoder(json.JSONEncoder):
    def default(self, obj):
        if isinstance(obj, np.integer):
            return int(obj)
        elif isinstance(obj, np.floating):
            return float(obj)
        elif isinstance(obj, np.ndarray):
            return obj.tolist()
        else:
            return super(MyEncoder, self).default(obj)


def ensure_dir(file_name):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(file_name), exist_ok=True)
    return file_name


def list_dirs(path=os.getcwd()):
    files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, '*'))
    files = [x for x in files if os.path.isdir(x)]
    return files


def file_exists(file_name, path_name=os.getcwd()):
    return os.path.isfile(os.path.join(path_name, file_name))


def write_json(json_obj, file_path):
    with open(file_path, 'w') as outfile:
        json.dump(json_obj, outfile, sort_keys=True, indent=4,
                  cls=MyNumpyEncoder)
    return json_obj


def load_json(file_path):
    with open(file_path, 'r') as infile:
        return json.load(infile)


def write_np(np_obj, file_path):
    with open(file_path, 'wb') as outfile:
        np.save(outfile, np_obj)

        "Sex": f"{100 * (df['sex'] == 'F').sum() / len(df):.1f}% F",

import pandas as pd

def summary_stats_group(df):
    """Return dict of summary stats for a DataFrame, including min and max age"""
    age_mean = df['age'].mean()
    age_std = df['age'].std()
    age_min = df['age'].min()
    age_max = df['age'].max()
    return {
        "Sample Size": f"{len(df)}",
        "Age": f"{age_mean:.2f} ± {age_std:.2f} [{age_min:.1f}, {age_max:.1f}]",
        "Sex": f"{100 * (df['sex'] == 'F').sum() / len(df):.1f}% F",
        "Avg. Thickness": f"{df['thickness'].mean():.2f} ± {df['thickness'].std():.2f}",
    }

datasets = demography_df['dataset'].unique()
splits = ['All Data', 'Train', 'Test']
metrics = ['Sample Size', 'Age', 'Sex', 'Avg. Thickness']

# MultiIndex columns: (split, metric)
cols = pd.MultiIndex.from_product([splits, metrics], names=['Split', 'Metric'])
summary_table = pd.DataFrame(index=datasets, columns=cols)

for dataset in datasets:
    df_dataset = demography_df[demography_df['dataset'] == dataset]

    # all_data
    stats_all = summary_stats_group(df_dataset)
    for metric, value in stats_all.items():
        summary_table.loc[dataset, ('All Data', metric)] = value

    # train
    df_train = df_dataset[df_dataset['split'] == 'Train']
    stats_train = summary_stats_group(df_train)
    for metric, value in stats_train.items():
        summary_table.loc[dataset, ('Train', metric)] = value

    # test
    df_test = df_dataset[df_dataset['split'] == 'Test']
    stats_test = summary_stats_group(df_test)
    for metric, value in stats_test.items():
        summary_table.loc[dataset, ('Test', metric)] = value

summary_table["Num Sites"] = [
    demography_df.loc[demography_df["dataset"] == dataset, "site"].nunique()
    for dataset in datasets
]

# Optional: ensure strings
summary_table = summary_table.astype(str)

summary_table.to_csv("/mountpoint/code/projects/normative_brain_charts/data/supplements/dataset_demography.csv")

def run_direct_model_for_feature(train_df, feature_name, overwrite=False):
    # Directory to store the model
    save_path = f"/mountpoint/code/projects/normative_brain_charts/data/pretrained_models/direct_models/{feature_name}_direct_model/"
    # If the directory was previously created
    if Path(save_path).exists():
        if overwrite:
            # Delete the directory
            print(f'Overwriting previous model: A direct model was stored at {save_path}!')
            shutil.rmtree(save_path)
        else:
            # Notify that file exists
            # print(f'Skipping direct model fit: The direct model is already stored at {save_path}!')
            return (feature_name, save_path, snm.DirectNormativeModel.load_model(Path(save_path)))
    
    # create a direct model
    normative_model = snm.DirectNormativeModel.load_model(
        Path("/mountpoint/code/projects/normative_brain_charts/data/pretrained_models/sample_direct_model/")
    )
    # update the variable of interest
    normative_model.spec.variable_of_interest = feature_name
    
    # create the parent save directory
    Path(save_path).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    
    # fit the model and save for later use
    with snm.utils.general.suppress_output():
        normative_model.fit(train_df, save_directory=Path(save_path), progress_bar=False,)
    
    return (feature_name, save_path, normative_model)

        # Skip if file exists and redo=False
        if not redo and Path(spectral_predictions_store_path).exists():
            continue
            
        else:
            if spectral_normative_model is None:
                # load an instance of the pretrained spectral model
                spectral_normative_model = snm.SpectralNormativeModel.load_model(
                    "/mountpoint/code/projects/normative_brain_charts/data/pretrained_models/rw1_full_spectral_model_10000/"
                )
        
            if train_spectral_basis_predictions is None:
                # memory mapped loading of precomputed spectral basis predictions
                train_spectral_basis_predictions_store_path = f'/mountpoint/code/projects/normative_brain_charts/data/predictions/spectral_basis/train:spectral_basis_predictions.joblib'
                train_spectral_basis_predictions = joblib.load(train_spectral_basis_predictions_store_path, mmap_mode="r")
        
            if test_spectral_basis_predictions is None:
                test_spectral_basis_predictions_store_path = f'/mountpoint/code/projects/normative_brain_charts/data/predictions/spectral_basis/test:spectral_basis_predictions.joblib'
                test_spectral_basis_predictions = joblib.load(test_spectral_basis_predictions_store_path, mmap_mode="r")

            with snm.utils.general.suppress_output():
                # run predicitons and save
                spectral_predictions={
                    'train': spectral_normative_model.predict(
                        encoded_query=query_signal_encoded[0,:n_k].reshape(n_k, 1),
                        spectral_predictions=train_spectral_basis_predictions,
                        n_modes=n_k,
                    ),
                    'test': spectral_normative_model.predict(
                        encoded_query=query_signal_encoded[0,:n_k].reshape(n_k, 1),
                        spectral_predictions=test_spectral_basis_predictions,
                        n_modes=n_k,
                    ),
                }

            # Ensure parent directories exist before save
            Path(spectral_predictions_store_path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            joblib.dump(spectral_predictions, spectral_predictions_store_path)
    
    return

from sklearn.preprocessing import normalize

# a function that turns a positive weighted vector to a weighted average operator (sum of weights will be scaled to 1)
def average_operator(signal):
    return normalize(signal.reshape(1,-1), norm='l1').reshape(-1)

# a function that turns a symmetric signal to a left vs. right signal
def left_right_difference_signal(signal):
    left_signal = signal[:left_cortical_surface_model.index_count]
    right_signal = signal[left_cortical_surface_model.index_count:]

    difference =  np.concatenate(
        [
            average_operator(left_signal),
            -average_operator(right_signal)
        ]
    )
    
    return difference

    kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=n_samples, n_init=5, random_state=random_state)
    labels = kmeans.fit_predict(points)
    centers = kmeans.cluster_centers_

    chosen = []
    for i, c in enumerate(centers):
        cluster_points = np.where(labels == i)[0]
        if len(cluster_points) == 0:
            continue
        dists = np.linalg.norm(points[cluster_points] - c, axis=1)
        chosen.append(cluster_points[np.argmin(dists)])
    return np.array(chosen, dtype=int)  # indices

# Given a known query, assuming the predictions of models are already stored on disk, compute evaluation metrics.
def evaluate_models_on_query(query_name, observed_train, observed_test, n_params):
    logger = snm.utils.general.get_logger(__name__)
    # logger.info('Starting...')
    # First get moments of observed values:
    baseline_mean = observed_train.mean()
    baseline_std = observed_train.std()
    # logger.info('Observations loaded...')
    
    # Dictionary containing stored prediction paths
    base_path = "/mountpoint/code/projects/normative_brain_charts/data/predictions"
    stored_predictions = {
        'direct': f"{base_path}/direct/{query_name}:direct_predictions.joblib",
        'spectral_10': f"{base_path}/spectral/{query_name}:spectral_predictions-N_10.joblib",
        'spectral_100': f"{base_path}/spectral/{query_name}:spectral_predictions-N_100.joblib",
        'spectral_1000': f"{base_path}/spectral/{query_name}:spectral_predictions-N_1000.joblib",
        'spectral_10000': f"{base_path}/spectral/{query_name}:spectral_predictions-N_10000.joblib",
    }
    
    # Dictionary to store evaluation metrics
    evaluations = {'train': {}, 'test': {}}
    
    for model in stored_predictions:
    # for model in tqdm(stored_predictions, desc="Model: "):
        predictions = joblib.load(stored_predictions[model])
        # reshape if needed
        predictions['train'].predictions['mu_estimate'] = predictions['train'].predictions['mu_estimate'].reshape(-1)
        predictions['train'].predictions['std_estimate'] = predictions['train'].predictions['std_estimate'].reshape(-1)
        predictions['test'].predictions['mu_estimate'] = predictions['test'].predictions['mu_estimate'].reshape(-1)
        predictions['test'].predictions['std_estimate'] = predictions['test'].predictions['std_estimate'].reshape(-1)
        # logger.info('predictions loaded')
        evaluations['train'][model] = predictions['train'].evaluate_predictions(
            variable_of_interest = observed_train,
            train_mean = baseline_mean,
            train_std = baseline_std,
            n_params = n_params
        ).evaluations
        # logger.info('train evaluations finished')
        evaluations['test'][model] = predictions['test'].evaluate_predictions(
            variable_of_interest = observed_test,
            train_mean = baseline_mean,
            train_std = baseline_std,
            n_params = n_params,
            msll_censored_quantile= 0.01,
        ).evaluations
        # logger.info('test evaluations finished')
    
    return (query_name, evaluations)

def plot_performance_distribution(data, key, ax, xmin, xmax, ymax, xtick_count, verbose=False):
    kde = stats.gaussian_kde(data[key])
    x_pad = (xmax - xmin) * 0.005
    x = np.linspace(xmin - x_pad, xmax + x_pad, 200)
    kde_values = kde(x)
    maxval = kde_values.max()
    kde_values /= maxval
    ax.fill_between(x, kde_values*0, kde_values, color=plotting_colors.get(key, '#333'), alpha=0.8)
    ax.plot(np.array([data[key].median(), data[key].median()]), np.array([0, kde(data[key].median())[0]/maxval]), color='#666', linewidth=2, alpha=0.5)
    ax.plot(x, kde_values, color=plotting_colors.get(key, '#333'), linewidth=2)
    ax.set_xlim(xmin - x_pad, xmax + x_pad)
    ax.set_ylim(0, ymax)
    ax.set_ylabel('')
    ax.text(
        0.98, 0.95, model_names[key], bbox=dict(facecolor='white', edgecolor=plotting_colors.get(key, '#333'), boxstyle='round,pad=0.4'),
        transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=16, ha='right')
    ax.spines['top'].set_color('none')
    ax.spines['right'].set_color('none')
    ax.spines['left'].set_color('none')
    ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.set_xticks(np.linspace(xmin, xmax, xtick_count))
    ax.tick_params(axis='both', labelsize=16, width=1., length=8)
    
    ax.grid(True, color='#999', linestyle='--', dashes=(3, 4), linewidth=1,)
    if verbose:
        print(f'Median performance, {key}: {data[key].median()}')
    
    # for ease of comparison
    if key != 'direct':
        ax.annotate(
            '', xy=(data['direct'].median(), 0.0), xytext=(data['direct'].median(), 0.3),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-|>', color=plotting_colors['direct'], linewidth=1., alpha=0.99, mutation_aspect=2.0, mutation_scale=25)
        )

def plot_compressed_performance_distribution(data, key, ax, xmin, xmax, ymax, xtick_count, verbose=False, flipped=True):
    kde = stats.gaussian_kde(data[key])
    x_pad = (xmax - xmin) * 0.005
    x = np.linspace(xmin - x_pad, xmax + x_pad, 200)
    kde_values = kde(x)
    maxval = kde_values.max()
    kde_values /= maxval
    mask = kde_values > 0.01
    ax.fill_betweenx(x[mask], kde_values[mask]*-1, kde_values[mask], color=plotting_colors.get(key, '#333'), alpha=0.8)
    ax.plot(
        np.array([-0.92*kde(data[key].median())[0]/maxval, 0.92*kde(data[key].median())[0]/maxval]),
        np.array([data[key].median(), data[key].median()]),
        color='#666', linewidth=4, alpha=0.7
    )
    ax.plot(
        np.array([-0.92*kde(data[key].quantile(0.25))[0]/maxval, 0.92*kde(data[key].quantile(0.25))[0]/maxval]),
        np.array([data[key].quantile(0.25), data[key].quantile(0.25)]),
        color='#666', linewidth=2., alpha=0.7, linestyle=':',
    )
    ax.plot(
        np.array([-0.92*kde(data[key].quantile(0.75))[0]/maxval, 0.92*kde(data[key].quantile(0.75))[0]/maxval]),
        np.array([data[key].quantile(0.75), data[key].quantile(0.75)]),
        color='#666', linewidth=2., alpha=0.7, linestyle=':',
    )
    ax.plot(kde_values[mask], x[mask], color=plotting_colors.get(key, '#333'), linewidth=2.5)
    ax.plot(-kde_values[mask], x[mask], color=plotting_colors.get(key, '#333'), linewidth=2.5)
    ax.set_ylim(xmin - x_pad, xmax + x_pad)
    ax.set_xlim(-ymax*1.5, ymax*1.5)
    ax.set_xlabel('')
    if flipped:
        ax.text(
            0.5, 0.98, model_names[key], bbox=dict(facecolor='white', edgecolor=plotting_colors.get(key, '#333'), boxstyle='round,pad=0.4'),

    ax.tick_params(axis='both', labelsize=16, width=1., length=8)
    
    ax.grid(True, color='#999', linestyle='--', dashes=(3, 4), linewidth=1,)
    if verbose:
        print(f'Median performance, {key}: {data[key].median()}')

    if key == 'direct':
        ax.annotate(
            '', xy=(1.1, data['direct'].median()), xytext=(1.5, data['direct'].median()), clip_on=False,
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-|>', color=plotting_colors['direct'], linewidth=1, alpha=0.99, mutation_aspect=1.2, mutation_scale=25)
        )
        ax.annotate(
            '', xy=(1.5, data['direct'].median()), xytext=(14.5, data['direct'].median()), clip_on=False,
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color=plotting_colors['direct'], linewidth=6, alpha=1., linestyle=(3, (0.05, 1.7)))
        )

def automated_comparison_evaluation_plotting(queries, store_dir='/mountpoint/code/projects/normative_brain_charts/figs/R1'):
    for query in tqdm(queries):
        for i, metric in enumerate(query['metrics']):
            # print(query, metric)
            # get the dataframe
            df = dataframe_dict[(query['spatial_extent'], metric)]
            options = []
            # symmetry
            if query['symmetry'] == 'symmetric':
                df = df[~df.index.str.contains('_asymmetry')]
                options.append('average')
            elif query['symmetry'] == 'asymmetric':
                df = df[df.index.str.contains('_asymmetry')]
                options.append(query['symmetry'])
            # regional atlas
            if query['spatial_extent'] == 'Regional':
                df= df[df.index.str.contains(query['atlas'])]
                options.append(query['atlas'])
            # high-resolution smoothing
            if query['spatial_extent'] == 'High-resolution':
                df= df[df.index.str.contains(f":{query['smoothing']}FWHM:")]
                options.append(f"{query['smoothing']} FWHM")
            # plot the figure
            option_text = f" ({', '.join(options)})" if len(options) > 0 else ""
            # title=f"{metric} of {query['spatial_extent'].lower()} queries{option_text}"
            title=""
            fig_name = f"comparative_evaluations_{query['spatial_extent']}_{metric}_" + '_'.join(options)
            metric_params = query['metric_params'][i]
            fig, axes = plot_comparative_evaluations(
                df=df.copy().dropna(), title=rf"\textbf{{{title}}}", xlabel=metric_name_dict[metric], **metric_params
            );
            # store the figure
            fig.savefig(ensure_dir(f'{store_dir}/subfigs/evals/{fig_name}.svg'), bbox_inches="tight")
            fig.savefig(ensure_dir(f'{store_dir}/subfigs/evals/{fig_name}.png'), bbox_inches="tight", dpi=600)
            plt.close(fig)

# uncomment to regenerate
automated_comparison_evaluation_plotting(queries)

def automated_comparison_evaluation_compressed_plotting(queries, store_dir='/mountpoint/code/projects/normative_brain_charts/figs/R1'):
    for query in tqdm(queries):
        for i, metric in enumerate(query['metrics']):
            # get the dataframe
            df = dataframe_dict[(query['spatial_extent'], metric)]
            options = []
            # symmetry
            if query['symmetry'] == 'symmetric':
                df = df[~df.index.str.contains('_asymmetry')]
                options.append('average')
            elif query['symmetry'] == 'asymmetric':
                df = df[df.index.str.contains('_asymmetry')]
                options.append(query['symmetry'])
            # regional atlas
            if query['spatial_extent'] == 'Regional':
                df= df[df.index.str.contains(query['atlas'])]
                options.append(query['atlas'])
            # high-resolution smoothing
            if query['spatial_extent'] == 'High-resolution':
                df= df[df.index.str.contains(f":{query['smoothing']}FWHM:")]
                options.append(f"{query['smoothing']} FWHM")
            # plot the figure
            option_text = f" ({', '.join(options)})" if len(options) > 0 else ""
            # title=f"{metric} of {query['spatial_extent'].lower()} queries{option_text}"
            title=""
            fig_name = f"compressed_comparative_evaluations_{query['spatial_extent']}_{metric}_" + '_'.join(options)
            metric_params = query['metric_params'][i]
            fig, axes = plot_compressed_comparative_evaluations(
                df=df.copy().dropna(), title=rf"\textbf{{{title}}}", xlabel=metric_name_dict[metric], **metric_params
            );
            # store the figure
            fig.savefig(ensure_dir(f'{store_dir}/subfigs/evals/{fig_name}.svg'), bbox_inches="tight")
            fig.savefig(ensure_dir(f'{store_dir}/subfigs/evals/{fig_name}.png'), bbox_inches="tight", dpi=600)
            # plt.show(fig)
            plt.close(fig)

    ax.set_visible(False)

    cax = inset_axes(
        ax,
        width="90%",
        height="90%",
        loc="center",
        bbox_to_anchor=(-0., 0.0, 1., 1.),
        bbox_transform=ax.transAxes,
        borderpad=0,
    )

    cb = fig.colorbar(
        mpl.cm.ScalarMappable(
            norm=mpl.colors.Normalize(vmin=lims[0], vmax=lims[1]),
            cmap=cmap
        ),
        cax=cax,
        aspect=10,
        orientation='horizontal',
    )

import numpy as np
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree
from scipy.sparse import csr_matrix

def build_gaussian_interpolation_matrix(base_coords, eval_coords, k=20, sigma=1.0, max_dist=None, eps=1e-12):
    """
    Build a sparse interpolation matrix using Gaussian kernel.
    
    Parameters
    ----------
    base_coords : (N, d) array
        Coordinates of known values.
    eval_coords : (M, d) array
        Coordinates where we want interpolated values.
    k : int
        Number of nearest neighbors.
    sigma : float
        Gaussian kernel bandwidth (controls locality).
    max_dist : float or None
        If not None, eval points farther than `max_dist` from all base points
        will be masked as NaN.
    eps : float
        Small value to avoid zero weights in Gaussian computation.
    
    Returns
    -------
    W : sparse CSR matrix, shape (M, N)
        Interpolation operator. Use as `eval_values = W @ base_values`.
    mask_nan : (M,) boolean array
        True where interpolation should be NaN.
    """
    M = eval_coords.shape[0]
    N = base_coords.shape[0]

    # Build KD-tree and query neighbors
    tree = cKDTree(base_coords)
    dists, idxs = tree.query(eval_coords, k=k)

    # Ensure 2D arrays
    if k == 1:
        dists = dists[:, None]
        idxs = idxs[:, None]

    # Compute Gaussian weights
    wi = np.exp(-(dists ** 2) / (2 * sigma ** 2)) + eps

    # Apply max_dist cutoff (exclude exact matches)
    if max_dist is not None:
        wi[dists > max_dist] = 0.0

    # Normalize weights per row (skip exact-match rows)
    row_sums = wi.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    nonzero_rows = (row_sums[:, 0] > 0)
    wi[nonzero_rows] /= row_sums[nonzero_rows]

    # Mask rows where all weights are zero
    mask_nan = wi.sum(axis=1) == 0

    # Build sparse interpolation matrix
    rows = np.repeat(np.arange(M), k)
    cols = idxs.ravel()
    data = wi.ravel()

    W = csr_matrix((data, (rows, cols)), shape=(M, N))

    return W, mask_nan


def interpolate(transform, base_values):
    W, mask_nan = transform
    eval_values = W @ base_values
    eval_values[mask_nan] = np.nan
    return eval_values

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Compute standardized mean squared error between cortical vectors
# x_vectors: (n, 59412)
# y_vectors: (m, n, 59412)  → compare n cortical vectors with m sets of n cortical vectors
# -------------------------------------------------------------
def generalized_smse(x_vectors, y_vectors):
    # variance per x-vector, kept 2D for broadcasting
    var = np.var(x_vectors, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    mse = np.mean((y_vectors - x_vectors[np.newaxis, :]) ** 2, axis=2)
    return mse / var.T  # shape: (m, n)


# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Compute generalized SMSE at different numbers of modes
# kernel: (59412, n_modes_total)
# signals: (k, 59412)
# n_modes: iterable of mode counts to test
# -------------------------------------------------------------
def generalized_smse_with_different_number_of_modes(kernel, signals, n_modes):
    encoded_signals = signals @ kernel  # (k, n_modes_total)
    k, n_total = encoded_signals.shape

    smse_list = []
    reconstructed = np.zeros_like(signals)
    prev_x = 0

    for x in tqdm(n_modes, desc="Modes", leave=False):
        # Incremental reconstruction to avoid recomputing from scratch
        delta_encoded = encoded_signals[:, prev_x:x]
        delta_kernel = kernel[:, prev_x:x]
        reconstructed += delta_encoded @ delta_kernel.T
        smse = generalized_smse(signals, reconstructed[np.newaxis, ...])[0]
        smse_list.append(smse)
        prev_x = x

    # Stack over all mode counts → shape (len(n_modes), n_signals)
    return np.stack(smse_list, axis=0).T


# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Chunked computation for large datasets
# -------------------------------------------------------------
def compute_generalized_smse_with_different_number_of_modes_in_chunks(
    kernel, signals, n_modes, chunk_size=100
):
    results = []

    for start in tqdm(range(0, signals.shape[0], chunk_size), desc="Chunks", leave=False):
        end = min(start + chunk_size, signals.shape[0])
        smse_chunk = generalized_smse_with_different_number_of_modes(
            kernel, signals[start:end], n_modes
        )
        results.append(smse_chunk)

    return np.concatenate(results, axis=0)

    all_signals = sparse.vstack([high_res_signals[k] for k in chunk_keys]).toarray()

    # Vectorized Math (Chunk Level)
    all_signals -= all_signals.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    signal_energies = np.power(all_signals, 2).sum(axis=1)

    # Matrix Multiplication for the chunk
    encoded_chunk = eigenmode_basis.encode(all_signals)

        # Assign back to the main projection vector
        comulative_energy_projection[j, chunk_cifti_indices] = prop_energies
    
    # Manual Cleanup to free memory
    del all_signals
    del encoded_chunk

def plotting_tasks(n_kernel = 1000):
    # Acquired thickness
    signal = thickness_data[individual_idx]
    lims=np.nanpercentile(predicted_moments['mu_estimate'], [1,99])
    yield joblib.delayed(generate_cortical_projection_plots)(
        fig_name=f'individual_thickness',
        lims=lims, colormap=cc.cm.rainbow_bgyrm_35_85_c71,
        brain_signal=signal, store_dir=store_dir,
    )
    # Smoothed thickness
    signal = smoothing_kernel_8mmFWHM.T @ signal
    smoothed_thickness = signal.copy()
    yield joblib.delayed(generate_cortical_projection_plots)(
        fig_name=f'smoothed_individual_thickness',
        lims=lims, colormap=cc.cm.rainbow_bgyrm_35_85_c71,
        brain_signal=signal, store_dir=store_dir,
    )
    # Reconstructed thickness
    # signal = (signal @ eigenmode_basis.eigenvectors[:n_kernel].T) @ eigenmode_basis.eigenvectors[:n_kernel]
    signal = eigenmode_basis.decode(eigenmode_basis.encode(signal, n_modes=n_kernel), n_modes=n_kernel)
    yield joblib.delayed(generate_cortical_projection_plots)(
        fig_name=f'reconstructed_smoothed_individual_thickness',
        lims=lims, colormap=cc.cm.rainbow_bgyrm_35_85_c71,
        brain_signal=signal, store_dir=store_dir,
    )
    
    # Normative Z score
    signal = (smoothed_thickness - individual_predicted_moments['mu_estimate'][0]) / individual_predicted_moments['std_estimate'][0]
    lims = [-4,4]
    yield joblib.delayed(generate_cortical_projection_plots)(
        fig_name=f'z_score_individual_thickness',
        lims=lims, colormap=cc.cm.coolwarm_r,
        brain_signal=signal, store_dir=store_dir,
    )
    
    # Colormap for centiles
    colors = cc.cm.diverging_gwr_55_95_c38_r((((np.linspace(-1, 1, 200))**7)/2)+0.5)
    effectmap = ListedColormap(colors)
    
    # Normative centiles
    signal = stats.norm.cdf(signal) * 100
    lims = [0,100]
    yield joblib.delayed(generate_cortical_projection_plots)(
        fig_name=f'centile_individual_thickness',
        lims=lims, colormap=effectmap,
        brain_signal=signal, store_dir=store_dir,
    )

import pandas as pd

def summary_stats_group(df):
    """Return dict of summary stats for a DataFrame"""
    return {
        "Sample Size": f"{len(df)}",
        "Age": f"{df['age'].mean():.2f} ± {df['age'].std():.2f}",
        "Sex": f"{100 * (df['sex'] == 'F').sum() / len(df):.1f}% F",
        "Avg. Thickness": f"{df['thickness'].mean():.2f} ± {df['thickness'].std():.2f}",
    }

metrics = ['Sample Size', 'Age', 'Sex', 'Avg. Thickness']

# MultiIndex columns: (split, metric)

    # all_data

    for metric, value in stats_all.items():

    # test
    df_test = df_dataset[df_dataset['split'] == 'Test']
    stats_test = summary_stats_group(df_test)
    for metric, value in stats_test.items():
        summary_table.loc[dataset, ('Test', metric)] = value

# Optional: ensure strings

def insert_2d_plot(i, j, axes, gs, image_path, title=None):
    ax = axes[i, j] = fig.add_subplot(gs[i, j])
    image = mpimg.imread(image_path)
    ax.imshow(image)
    ax.axis('off')
    # ax.xaxis.set_visible(False)
    # ax.yaxis.set_visible(False)
    if title is not None:
        ax.text(0.51, 1.0, title, transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=20, ha='center', va='center')
    return ax

def insert_multiple_cortical_images(i, j, axes, gs, image_paths, cbar_image_path=None):
    ax = axes[i, j] = fig.add_subplot(gs[i, j])
    ax.axis('off')
    # ax.xaxis.set_visible(False)
    # ax.yaxis.set_visible(False)
    for k, image_path in enumerate(image_paths):
        iax = ax.inset_axes((0.0, 0.79 - k*0.176, 1., 0.176))
        image = mpimg.imread(image_path)
        iax.imshow(image)
        # iax.text(0.5, 0.5, xlabel, transform=iax.transAxes, fontsize=18, ha='center', va='center')
        iax.axis('off')
        # iax.xaxis.set_visible(False)
        # iax.yaxis.set_visible(False)
    if cbar_image_path is not None:
        iax = ax.inset_axes((0.0, 0.0, 1., 0.1))
        image = mpimg.imread(cbar_image_path)
        iax.imshow(image)
        # iax.text(0.5, 0.5, xlabel, transform=iax.transAxes, fontsize=18, ha='center', va='center')
        iax.axis('off')
        # iax.xaxis.set_visible(False)
        # iax.yaxis.set_visible(False)
    return ax

class MyNumpyEncoder(json.JSONEncoder):
    def default(self, obj):
        if isinstance(obj, np.integer):
            return int(obj)
        elif isinstance(obj, np.floating):
            return float(obj)
        elif isinstance(obj, np.ndarray):
            return obj.tolist()
        else:
            return super(MyEncoder, self).default(obj)

import warnings

warnings.simplefilter('ignore', PILImage.DecompressionBombWarning)

def show_image(image_path, width=1000, resample=PILImage.LANCZOS):
    """
    Display an image in Jupyter at a fixed width while preserving aspect ratio.
    The image is resampled (not embedded full-size) to reduce notebook memory.
    """
    img = PILImage.open(image_path).copy()
    w, h = img.size
    new_h = int(h * width / w)
    img = img.resize((width, new_h), resample)
    display(img)

def crop_image(image_path, start_x, start_y, end_x, end_y):
    """Crop a saved image by fractional coordinates (0-1)."""
    img = PILImage.open(image_path)
    w, h = img.size
    box = (int(start_x * w), int(start_y * h), int(end_x * w), int(end_y * h))
    img.crop(box).save(image_path)

def gaussian_transformation(data, mu, sigma):
    return stats.norm(loc=mu, scale=sigma).pdf(data)

def signal_to_centile(signal):
    return ((stats.rankdata(signal, method='average') - 1) / (len(signal) - 1)) * 100

# a function that turns a set of positive weighted vectors to a weighted average operator (sum of weights will be scaled to 1)
def average_operator(signals):
    return sklearn.preprocessing.normalize(signals, norm='l1', axis=1)
