import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.gridspec import GridSpec

FS_TITLE = 18
FS_AXLABEL = 16
FS_TICK = 16
FS_LEGEND = 16
FS_PANEL = 20


def plot_gap_statistic(gap_results, figsize=(20, 9), annotate=True):
    """Two-panel summary of the gap statistic analysis."""
    k_vals = np.asarray(gap_results['k_values'])
    gap = np.asarray(gap_results['gap'])
    gap_se = np.asarray(gap_results['gap_se'])
    k_opt = gap_results['optimal_k_tibshirani']

    lower = gap - gap_se               # Gap(k) - SE(k)
    gap1 = gap[0]

    fig = plt.figure(figsize=figsize)
    gs = GridSpec(1, 3, figure=fig, wspace=0.3)

    # --- Panel A: gap profile -------------------------------------------
    ax_a = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, :2])
    ax_a.axhspan(lower[1:].max(), gap1, color='#d04444', alpha=0.10, zorder=0)
    ax_a.axhline(gap1, color='#d04444', ls='--', lw=1.6, zorder=1,
                 label=r'Gap$(1)$')
    ax_a.hlines(lower[1:], k_vals[1:] - 0.28, k_vals[1:] + 0.28,
                color='#d04444', ls=':', lw=1.8, zorder=2,
                label=r'Gap$(k) - $SE$(k)$')
    ax_a.errorbar(k_vals, gap, yerr=gap_se, marker='o', capsize=5,
                  color='C0', markersize=9, lw=1.8, markeredgecolor='black',
                  markeredgewidth=0.8, zorder=3, label=r'Gap$(k) \pm$ SE')
    i_opt = int(np.where(k_vals == k_opt)[0][0])
    ax_a.plot(k_vals[i_opt], gap[i_opt], 'o', markersize=20,
              markerfacecolor='none', markeredgecolor='#d04444',
              markeredgewidth=2.5, zorder=5)
    ax_a.set_xlabel('Number of clusters ($k$)', fontsize=FS_AXLABEL)
    ax_a.set_ylabel('Gap statistic', fontsize=FS_AXLABEL)
    ax_a.set_xticks(k_vals)
    ax_a.tick_params(labelsize=FS_TICK)
    ax_a.set_title('Gap statistic across $k$', fontsize=FS_TITLE)
    ax_a.grid(alpha=0.25, axis='y')
    ax_a.set_axisbelow(True)
    ax_a.legend(loc='upper right', fontsize=FS_LEGEND, frameon=True)
    if annotate:
        ax_a.text(0.03, 0.06,
                  rf'Selection rule satisfied at $k^\ast = {k_opt}$;' '\n'
                  r'no higher $k$ distinguishable from 1',
                  transform=ax_a.transAxes, fontsize=FS_LEGEND, ha='left',
                  va='bottom', color='#d04444',
                  bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.5', facecolor='white',
                            edgecolor='#d04444', alpha=0.9))

    # --- Panel B: generalised selection criterion -----------------------
    ax_b = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
    k_check = k_vals[1:]
    crit = gap1 - lower[1:]
    cols = ['#3a9b3a' if q >= 0 else '#d04444' for q in crit]
    ax_b.bar(k_check, crit, color=cols, alpha=0.8, edgecolor='black', lw=0.8)
    ax_b.axhline(0, color='black', lw=1.2)
    ax_b.set_xlabel('$k$', fontsize=FS_AXLABEL)
    ax_b.set_ylabel(r'Gap$(1) -$ [Gap$(k) - $SE$(k)$]', fontsize=FS_AXLABEL)
    ax_b.set_xticks(k_check)
    ax_b.tick_params(labelsize=FS_TICK)
    ax_b.set_title('Selection rule criterion', fontsize=FS_TITLE)
    ax_b.grid(alpha=0.25, axis='y')
    ax_b.set_axisbelow(True)

    for ax, L in ((ax_a, 'A'), (ax_b, 'B')):
        ax.annotate(rf'$\mathbf{{{L}}}$', xy=(0, 1), xycoords='axes fraction',
                    xytext=(-45, 5), textcoords='offset points',
                    fontsize=FS_PANEL, va='bottom', ha='left')
    return fig

import numpy as np
from scipy.cluster.hierarchy import linkage, fcluster
from scipy.optimize import linear_sum_assignment
from joblib import Parallel, delayed
from tqdm.auto import tqdm


def jaccard(set_a, set_b):
    """Jaccard similarity between two sets of indices."""
    if len(set_a) == 0 and len(set_b) == 0:
        return 1.0
    intersection = len(set_a & set_b)
    union = len(set_a | set_b)
    return intersection / union if union > 0 else 0.0


def match_clusters_hungarian(orig_labels, boot_labels, boot_indices, n_clusters):
    """
    Match bootstrap clusters to original clusters via Hungarian assignment on Jaccard.
    
    Parameters
    ----------
    orig_labels : (n_samples,) array
        Cluster labels from clustering the FULL dataset.
    boot_labels : (n_boot,) array
        Cluster labels from clustering the bootstrap subsample.
    boot_indices : (n_boot,) array
        Original-data indices of the bootstrap samples (in order).
    n_clusters : int
        Number of clusters.
    
    Returns
    -------
    matched_jaccards : (n_clusters,) array
        For each original cluster k, the Jaccard similarity with its best-matched
        bootstrap cluster, considering only samples present in the bootstrap.
    """
    boot_indices_set = set(boot_indices.tolist())
    
    # Sets per original cluster (restricted to bootstrap samples)
    orig_sets = []
    for k in range(n_clusters):
        members = np.where(orig_labels == k)[0]
        members_in_boot = set(members.tolist()) & boot_indices_set
        orig_sets.append(members_in_boot)
    
    # Sets per bootstrap cluster (mapped back to original-index space)
    boot_sets = []
    for k in range(n_clusters):
        members_boot_positions = np.where(boot_labels == k)[0]
        members_orig_idx = set(boot_indices[members_boot_positions].tolist())
        boot_sets.append(members_orig_idx)
    
    # Jaccard cost matrix (negative for Hungarian which minimises)
    cost = np.zeros((n_clusters, n_clusters))
    for i in range(n_clusters):
        for j in range(n_clusters):
            cost[i, j] = -jaccard(orig_sets[i], boot_sets[j])
    
    row_ind, col_ind = linear_sum_assignment(cost)
    return np.array([-cost[r, c] for r, c in zip(row_ind, col_ind)])


def cluster_data(data, n_clusters, linkage_method='ward'):
    """Hierarchical clustering returning 0-indexed labels."""
    Z = linkage(data, method=linkage_method)
    return fcluster(Z, t=n_clusters, criterion='maxclust') - 1


def single_bootstrap_iteration(seed, data, orig_labels, n_clusters, linkage_method, n_samples):
    """One bootstrap draw and per-cluster Jaccard assessment."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    boot_indices = rng.integers(0, n_samples, size=n_samples)
    boot_data = data[boot_indices]
    boot_labels = cluster_data(boot_data, n_clusters, linkage_method)
    return match_clusters_hungarian(orig_labels, boot_labels, boot_indices, n_clusters)


def hennig_cluster_stability(
    data, k_values=range(2, 7), linkage_method='ward',
    n_bootstrap=1000, n_jobs=1, random_seed=0,
):
    """
    Bootstrap cluster stability assessment per Hennig (2007).
    
    Parameters
    ----------
    data : (n_samples, n_features) array
    k_values : iterable of cluster counts to test
    linkage_method : str, passed to scipy.cluster.hierarchy.linkage
    n_bootstrap : int, number of bootstrap iterations per k
    n_jobs : parallelism level
    random_seed : base seed for reproducibility
    
    Returns
    -------
    results : dict
        Keys are k values; values are dicts with:
            'per_cluster_mean'   : (k,) mean Jaccard per cluster
            'per_cluster_median' : (k,) median Jaccard per cluster
            'per_cluster_q25'    : (k,) 25th percentile per cluster
            'per_cluster_q75'    : (k,) 75th percentile per cluster
            'all_jaccards'       : (n_bootstrap, k) raw Jaccards
            'mean_overall'       : scalar mean across all clusters
    """
    data = np.asarray(data, dtype=float)
    n_samples = data.shape[0]
    results = {}
    
    for k in k_values:
        print(f"\n=== k = {k} ===")
        orig_labels = cluster_data(data, k, linkage_method)
        sizes = np.bincount(orig_labels, minlength=k)
        print(f"  Cluster sizes: {sizes.tolist()}")
        
        jaccards = Parallel(n_jobs=n_jobs)(
            delayed(single_bootstrap_iteration)(
                random_seed + b, data, orig_labels, k, linkage_method, n_samples,
            )
            for b in tqdm(range(n_bootstrap), desc=f"Bootstrap k={k}", leave=False)
        )
        jaccards = np.array(jaccards)  # (n_bootstrap, k)
        
        per_cluster_mean = jaccards.mean(axis=0)
        results[k] = {
            'per_cluster_mean': per_cluster_mean,
            'per_cluster_median': np.median(jaccards, axis=0),
            'per_cluster_q25': np.percentile(jaccards, 25, axis=0),
            'per_cluster_q75': np.percentile(jaccards, 75, axis=0),
            'all_jaccards': jaccards,
            'mean_overall': per_cluster_mean.mean(),
        }
        
        print(f"  Per-cluster mean Jaccard: {per_cluster_mean.round(3).tolist()}")
        print(f"  Hennig interpretation:")
        for c, j in enumerate(per_cluster_mean):
            if j < 0.5:
                tag = "DISSOLVED (no real structure)"
            elif j < 0.6:
                tag = "weak pattern at best"
            elif j < 0.75:
                tag = "pattern but not globally stable"
            elif j < 0.85:
                tag = "stable cluster"
            else:
                tag = "highly stable cluster"
            print(f"    Cluster {c} (n={sizes[c]}): Jaccard={j:.3f} -- {tag}")
    
    return results

%matplotlib agg

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.gridspec import GridSpec
from scipy.optimize import linear_sum_assignment

BANDS = [(0.00, 0.50, '#fdd', 'dissolved'), (0.50, 0.60, '#fed', 'weak'),
         (0.60, 0.75, '#ffd', 'pattern'), (0.75, 0.85, '#dfd', 'stable'),
         (0.85, 1.00, '#cfc', 'highly stable')]
STABLE_T, DISSOLVED_T = 0.75, 0.50

FS_TITLE = 18
FS_AXLABEL = 16
FS_TICK = 16
FS_BAND = 16
FS_LEGEND = 16
FS_PANEL = 20


def get_iteration_jaccards_and_labels(data, orig_labels, n_clusters, seed,
                                      linkage_method='ward'):
    """Re-run one bootstrap iteration, returning indices, matched labels, Jaccards."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    boot_indices = rng.integers(0, len(data), size=len(data))
    boot_labels = cluster_data(data[boot_indices], n_clusters, linkage_method)
    jaccards = match_clusters_hungarian(orig_labels, boot_labels, boot_indices,
                                        n_clusters)
    boot_set = set(boot_indices.tolist())
    orig_sets = [set(np.where(orig_labels == k)[0].tolist()) & boot_set
                 for k in range(n_clusters)]
    boot_sets = [set(boot_indices[boot_labels == k].tolist())
                 for k in range(n_clusters)]
    cost = np.array([[-jaccard(o, b) for b in boot_sets] for o in orig_sets])
    _, col_ind = linear_sum_assignment(cost)
    relabel = np.full(n_clusters, -1, dtype=int)
    for orig_c, boot_c in enumerate(col_ind):
        relabel[boot_c] = orig_c
    return boot_indices, relabel[boot_labels], jaccards


def _palette(k):
    return plt.cm.tab10(np.linspace(0, 1, max(10, k))[:k])


def _strip_axes(ax):
    """Remove ticks and labels, keeping the frame."""
    ax.set_xticks([])
    ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.set_xlabel('')
    ax.set_ylabel('')


def _jaccard_panel(ax, results, title, band_labels=True):
    ks = sorted(results.keys())
    for lo, hi, col, _ in BANDS:
        ax.axhspan(lo, hi, color=col, alpha=0.5, zorder=0)
    for t in (DISSOLVED_T, STABLE_T):
        ax.axhline(t, color='gray', ls='--', lw=0.8, zorder=1)
    cmap = plt.cm.viridis(np.linspace(0.1, 0.9, len(ks)))
    for i, k in enumerate(ks):
        m = results[k]['per_cluster_mean']
        q25, q75 = results[k]['per_cluster_q25'], results[k]['per_cluster_q75']
        x = np.full(k, i, dtype=float) + (np.linspace(-0.22, 0.22, k) if k > 1 else 0)
        for c in range(k):
            ax.plot([x[c], x[c]], [q25[c], q75[c]], color=cmap[i], lw=1.4, zorder=2)
        ax.scatter(x, m, s=95, color=cmap[i], edgecolor='black', lw=0.8, zorder=3)
        mj = float(np.mean(m))
        ax.plot([i - 0.30, i + 0.30], [mj, mj], ls='--', lw=1.8,
                color=cmap[i], zorder=5)
        ax.text(i - 0.32, mj + 0.0, rf'$\bar{{J}}={mj:.2f}$', ha='right',
                va='center', fontsize=FS_BAND * 1.1, color='0.15', zorder=6,
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.4', fc=[1, 1, 1, 0.3], ec=cmap[i],
                          lw=1.2, alpha=0.99))
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(ks)))
    ax.set_xticklabels([f'$k={k}$' for k in ks], fontsize=FS_TICK)
    ax.tick_params(axis='x', direction='out', pad=0.1 * FS_TICK)
    ax.tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=FS_TICK)
    ax.set_ylabel('Jaccard Similarity', fontsize=FS_AXLABEL)
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
    ax.set_xlim(-0.65, len(ks) - 0.5 + (0.12 if band_labels else 0))
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=FS_TITLE)
    if band_labels:
        for lo, hi, _, lab in BANDS:
            ax.text(len(ks) - 0.4, (lo + hi) / 2, lab, fontsize=FS_BAND,
                    va='center', ha='right', color='#555')


def _assignment_panel(axes, data_2d, results, ks, linkage_method):
    for ax, k in zip(axes, ks):
        labels = cluster_data(data_2d, k, linkage_method)
        cmap, m = _palette(k), results[k]['per_cluster_mean']
        for c in range(k):
            msk = labels == c
            ax.scatter(data_2d[msk, 0], data_2d[msk, 1], color=cmap[c], s=18,
                       alpha=0.75, edgecolor='black', lw=0.25,
                       label=f'$n={msk.sum()}$, $J={m[c]:.2f}$')
        ax.set_title(f'$k={k}$', fontsize=FS_TITLE)
        ax.legend(fontsize=FS_LEGEND, loc='best', frameon=True, handlelength=0.8,
                  borderpad=0.3, labelspacing=0.25, handletextpad=0.4)
        _strip_axes(ax)


def _bootstrap_panel(axes, data_2d, k_ex, linkage_method, n_search, seed):
    orig = cluster_data(data_2d, k_ex, linkage_method)
    cmap = _palette(k_ex)
    draws = []
    for b in range(n_search):
        bi, bl, jv = get_iteration_jaccards_and_labels(
            data_2d, orig, k_ex, seed + b, linkage_method)
        draws.append((float(np.mean(jv)), bi, bl))
    draws.sort(key=lambda t: t[0])
    picks = [('Low stability', draws[len(draws) // 10]),
             ('Median stability', draws[len(draws) // 2]),
             ('High stability', draws[-max(1, len(draws) // 10)])]
    for c in range(k_ex):
        msk = orig == c
        axes[0].scatter(data_2d[msk, 0], data_2d[msk, 1], color=cmap[c], s=18,
                        alpha=0.8, edgecolor='black', lw=0.25)
    axes[0].set_title(f'Full sample; $k={k_ex}$', fontsize=FS_TITLE)
    for ax, (lab, (mj, bi, bl)) in zip(axes[1:], picks):
        for c in range(k_ex):
            msk = bl == c
            if not msk.any():
                continue
            pts = data_2d[bi[msk]]
            ax.scatter(pts[:, 0], pts[:, 1], color=cmap[c], s=18, alpha=0.8,
                       edgecolor='black', lw=0.25)
        ax.set_title(f'{lab}; mean $J={mj:.2f}$', fontsize=FS_TITLE)
    for ax in axes:
        _strip_axes(ax)


def plot_clusterability_summary(
        results_mds, results_pca10, results_pca20, data_2d,
        ks_to_show=(2, 3, 4, 5), k_example=2, linkage_method='ward',
        n_bootstrap_search=1000, random_seed=0, figsize=(20, 28)):
    """Five-panel summary of bootstrap cluster stability."""
    ncols = max(len(ks_to_show), 4)
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=figsize)
    gs = GridSpec(5, ncols, figure=fig,
                  height_ratios=[1.2, 1.0, 1.0, 1.2, 1.2],
                  hspace=0.2, wspace=0.15)

    ax_a = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, :])
    _jaccard_panel(ax_a, results_mds,
                   'Bootstrap cluster stability in the two-dimensional '
                   'heterogeneity landscape (MDS)')

    axes_b = [fig.add_subplot(gs[1, i]) for i in range(len(ks_to_show))]
    for ax in axes_b[1:]:
        ax.sharex(axes_b[0]); ax.sharey(axes_b[0])
    _assignment_panel(axes_b, data_2d, results_mds, ks_to_show, linkage_method)

    axes_c = [fig.add_subplot(gs[2, i]) for i in range(4)]
    for ax in axes_c[1:]:
        ax.sharex(axes_c[0]); ax.sharey(axes_c[0])
    _bootstrap_panel(axes_c, data_2d, k_example, linkage_method,
                     n_bootstrap_search, random_seed)

    ax_d = fig.add_subplot(gs[3, :])
    ax_e = fig.add_subplot(gs[4, :])
    _jaccard_panel(ax_d, results_pca10, 'Replication: Ten-component PCA', band_labels=True)
    _jaccard_panel(ax_e, results_pca20, 'Replication: Twenty-component PCA', band_labels=True)

    for ax, L in ((ax_a, 'A'), (axes_b[0], 'B'), (axes_c[0], 'C'),
                  (ax_d, 'D'), (ax_e, 'E')):
        ax.annotate(rf'$\mathbf{{{L}}}$', xy=(0, 1), xycoords='axes fraction',
                    xytext=(-45, 5), textcoords='offset points',
                    fontsize=FS_PANEL, va='bottom', ha='left')
    return fig

import numpy as np
from scipy.cluster.hierarchy import linkage, fcluster
from joblib import Parallel, delayed
from tqdm.auto import tqdm


def cluster_ward(data, k):
    Z = linkage(data, method='ward')
    return fcluster(Z, t=k, criterion='maxclust') - 1


def assign_to_nearest_centroid(data, centroids):
    dists = np.linalg.norm(data[:, None, :] - centroids[None, :, :], axis=2)
    return dists.argmin(axis=1)


def co_membership_matrix(labels):
    """
    Build a (n, n) boolean matrix M where M[i, j] = True iff labels[i] == labels[j].
    Used for the prediction strength pair-counting.
    """
    return labels[:, None] == labels[None, :]


def single_prediction_strength_iteration(seed, data, k):
    """
    One iteration of prediction strength per Tibshirani & Walther 2005.
    
    1. Split data in half (A and B).
    2. Cluster each half independently at k.
    3. Use centroids from A to assign labels to B's subjects (i.e. predict B's clustering from A).
    4. For each cluster c in B's *own* clustering, count the fraction of pairs of B-subjects in
       cluster c that *also* end up in the same cluster under A's centroid-based assignment.
    5. The prediction strength of this iteration is the MINIMUM such fraction across clusters.
       (Tibshirani's "weakest cluster" criterion.)
    6. Repeat with roles of A and B swapped.
    
    Returns: (ps_AtoB, ps_BtoA)
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    n = data.shape[0]
    perm = rng.permutation(n)
    half = n // 2
    idx_A = perm[:half]
    idx_B = perm[half:2 * half]  # ensure equal sizes
    
    data_A = data[idx_A]
    data_B = data[idx_B]
    
    labels_A = cluster_ward(data_A, k)
    labels_B = cluster_ward(data_B, k)
    
    # Centroids of each half's own clustering
    centroids_A = np.array([data_A[labels_A == c].mean(axis=0) for c in range(k)])
    centroids_B = np.array([data_B[labels_B == c].mean(axis=0) for c in range(k)])
    
    # Direction 1: use A's centroids to classify B
    labels_B_via_A = assign_to_nearest_centroid(data_B, centroids_A)
    
    # For each cluster c in B's own clustering, compute the fraction of pairs in c
    # that are also together under A's classification
    min_ps_B = 1.0
    for c in range(k):
        members = np.where(labels_B == c)[0]
        if len(members) < 2:
            # Singleton or empty cluster: skip (or assign 1 — Tibshirani is ambiguous;
            # most implementations skip)
            continue
        # Fraction of pairs from members that are co-classified under labels_B_via_A
        coassigned = co_membership_matrix(labels_B_via_A[members])
        # Upper triangle (i < j), exclude diagonal
        n_pairs = len(members) * (len(members) - 1) // 2
        n_same = (coassigned.sum() - len(members)) // 2
        frac = n_same / n_pairs
        min_ps_B = min(min_ps_B, frac)
    
    # Direction 2: use B's centroids to classify A
    labels_A_via_B = assign_to_nearest_centroid(data_A, centroids_B)
    min_ps_A = 1.0
    for c in range(k):
        members = np.where(labels_A == c)[0]
        if len(members) < 2:
            continue
        coassigned = co_membership_matrix(labels_A_via_B[members])
        n_pairs = len(members) * (len(members) - 1) // 2
        n_same = (coassigned.sum() - len(members)) // 2
        frac = n_same / n_pairs
        min_ps_A = min(min_ps_A, frac)
    
    return min_ps_A, min_ps_B


def prediction_strength(
    data, k_values=range(2, 7),
    n_iterations=500, n_jobs=1, random_seed=0,
    threshold=0.8,
):
    """
    Prediction strength per Tibshirani & Walther 2005.
    
    Tibshirani's recommendation for selecting k:
        k* = largest k such that PS(k) >= threshold (default 0.8 or 0.9)
        If PS(k) < threshold for all k > 1, the data is best described as 1 cluster.
    
    Returns dict keyed by k, with mean/median/IQR of prediction strength across iterations.
    """
    data = np.asarray(data, dtype=float)
    results = {}
    
    for k in k_values:
        print(f"\n=== k = {k} ===")
        ps_pairs = Parallel(n_jobs=n_jobs)(
            delayed(single_prediction_strength_iteration)(random_seed + b, data, k)
            for b in tqdm(range(n_iterations), desc=f"PS k={k}", leave=False)
        )
        all_ps = np.array([p for pair in ps_pairs for p in pair])
        results[k] = {
            'distribution': all_ps,
            'mean':   all_ps.mean(),
            'median': np.median(all_ps),
            'q25':    np.percentile(all_ps, 25),
            'q75':    np.percentile(all_ps, 75),
        }
        print(f"  Mean PS:   {results[k]['mean']:.3f}")
        print(f"  Median PS: {results[k]['median']:.3f}")
        print(f"  IQR:       [{results[k]['q25']:.3f}, {results[k]['q75']:.3f}]")
        
        if results[k]['mean'] >= threshold:
            print(f"  Above threshold {threshold} → k = {k} indicates real cluster structure")
        else:
            print(f"  Below threshold {threshold} → k = {k} does not indicate real cluster structure")
    
    # Tibshirani's k-selection rule: largest k above threshold (or 1 if none)
    above_threshold = [k for k, r in results.items() if r['mean'] >= threshold]
    if above_threshold:
        k_optimal = max(above_threshold)
    else:
        k_optimal = 1
    print(f"\nOptimal k by Tibshirani's threshold ({threshold}): {k_optimal}")
    
    return results, k_optimal

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

FS_TITLE = 18
FS_AXLABEL = 16
FS_TICK = 16
FS_LEGEND = 18
FS_PANEL = 20

THRESH, STRICT = 0.8, 0.9


def plot_prediction_strength(ps_results, figsize=(12, 8), panel_label=None,
                             show_median=False):
    """Mean prediction strength across k, with interquartile spread."""
    ks = sorted(ps_results.keys())
    means = np.array([ps_results[k]['mean'] for k in ks])
    q25 = np.array([ps_results[k]['q25'] for k in ks])
    q75 = np.array([ps_results[k]['q75'] for k in ks])

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
    ax.axhspan(THRESH, 1.0, color='#3a9b3a', alpha=0.08, zorder=0)
    ax.axhline(THRESH, color='#d04444', ls='--', lw=1.6, zorder=1,
               label=f'Threshold ({THRESH})')
    ax.axhline(STRICT, color='#e08a1e', ls=':', lw=1.8, zorder=1,
               label=f'Strict threshold ({STRICT})')

    for k, lo, hi in zip(ks, q25, q75):
        ax.plot([k, k], [lo, hi], color='C0', lw=1.6, zorder=2,
                solid_capstyle='round')
    # ax.plot(ks, means, '-', color='C0', lw=1.8, zorder=2)
    ax.scatter(ks, means, s=95, color='C0', edgecolor='black', lw=0.8,
               zorder=3, label='Mean prediction strength')
    if show_median:
        meds = np.array([ps_results[k]['median'] for k in ks])
        ax.scatter(ks, meds, marker='_', s=220, color='0.15', lw=1.6,
                   zorder=4, label='Median')

    # proxy handle for the IQR line
    ax.scatter([], [], marker='|', s=260, color='C0', linewidths=1.8,
               label='Interquartile range')

    ax.set_xticks(ks)
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=FS_TICK)
    ax.set_xlabel('Number of clusters ($k$)', fontsize=FS_AXLABEL)
    ax.set_ylabel('Prediction strength', fontsize=FS_AXLABEL)
    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.02)
    ax.set_title('Prediction strength across $k$', fontsize=FS_TITLE)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.25, axis='y')
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    ax.legend(loc='lower left', fontsize=FS_LEGEND, frameon=True)

    if panel_label:
        ax.annotate(rf'$\mathbf{{{panel_label}}}$', xy=(0, 1),
                    xycoords='axes fraction', xytext=(-45, 5),
                    textcoords='offset points', fontsize=FS_PANEL,
                    va='bottom', ha='left')
    return fig

SigClust2 (Kimes et al. 2017) tests, at each split of a hierarchical clustering, whether the data are better described by two clusters than by a single Gaussian, controlling the family-wise error rate across the dendrogram. It is R-only, so this step runs outside the Python environment: the R script reads the parquet files exported above and writes results back as CSV for the cells below.

    r-base=4.4 r-arrow r-devtools

      pak::pak("pkimes/sigclust2@e86ded76aa8c21c92d9621f58740d102dfa712a4")'

Run (~1.5 min)

The script covers both representations (2D MDS landscape, 20-component PCA) under two null-generating algorithms: hclust, recommended for Euclidean distance and treated as primary, and 2means, which gives conservative p-values and serves as a robustness check.

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.gridspec import GridSpec

FS_TITLE = 18
FS_AXLABEL = 16
FS_TICK = 16
FS_LEGEND = 18
FS_PANEL = 20

def _strip(ax):
    ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.set_xlabel(''); ax.set_ylabel('')


def plot_sigclust2(summary, ci_nulls, data_2d, k2_labels,
                   partitions=(('mds', '2D MDS landscape'),
                               ('pca', '20-component PCA')),
                   order=('mds', 'pca', 'mds_2means', 'pca_2means'),
                   figsize=(20, 18), alpha_level=0.05):
    """k = 2 partitions tested (top), and the null cluster-index
    distributions against which they were assessed (below).

    Columns correspond to representation, rows below the top to null algorithm.
    """
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=figsize)
    gs = GridSpec(3, 2, figure=fig, height_ratios=[1.8, 1.0, 1.0],
                  hspace=0.28, wspace=0.16)
    summary = summary.set_index('config')
    pal = plt.cm.tab10(np.linspace(0, 1, 10))[:2]
    letters = iter(['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E', 'F'])

    def _label(ax):
        ax.annotate(rf'$\mathbf{{{next(letters)}}}$', xy=(0, 1),
                    xycoords='axes fraction', xytext=(-45, 5),
                    textcoords='offset points', fontsize=FS_PANEL,
                    va='bottom', ha='left')

    # --- Top row: the partitions that were tested -----------------------
    for j, (cfg, title) in enumerate(partitions):
        ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, j])
        lab = np.asarray(k2_labels[cfg])
        for c, u in enumerate(np.unique(lab)):
            m = lab == u
            ax.scatter(data_2d[m, 0], data_2d[m, 1], s=26, color=pal[c],
                       alpha=0.8, edgecolor='black', linewidth=0.3,
                       label=f'$n = {m.sum()}$')
        ax.set_title(f'{title}: $k=2$ partition', fontsize=FS_TITLE)
        ax.legend(loc='best', fontsize=FS_LEGEND * 1., frameon=True,
                  handlelength=0.9, borderpad=0.35, labelspacing=0.3)
        _strip(ax)
        _label(ax)

    # --- Lower rows: null distributions ---------------------------------
    for i, cfg in enumerate(order):
        row = summary.loc[cfg]
        null = np.asarray(ci_nulls[cfg])
        ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[1 + i // 2, i % 2])

        ax.hist(null, bins=60, color='0.65', edgecolor='none', alpha=0.85,
                label='Null distribution')
        ax.axvline(row['ci_obs'], color='#d04444', lw=2.2, zorder=4,
                   label='Observed cluster index')
        q_alpha = float(np.quantile(null, alpha_level))
        xlo, xhi = ax.get_xlim()
        ax.axvspan(xlo, q_alpha, color='#d04444', alpha=0.10, zorder=0,
                   label=f'Rejection ($\\alpha<{alpha_level}$)')
        ax.axvline(q_alpha, color='#d04444', ls=':', lw=1.4, zorder=1)
        ax.set_xlim(xlo, xhi)

        ax.set_title(row['label'], fontsize=FS_TITLE)
        ax.set_xlabel('2-means cluster index', fontsize=FS_AXLABEL)
        ax.set_ylabel('Simulated datasets', fontsize=FS_AXLABEL)
        ax.tick_params(labelsize=FS_TICK)
        ax.text(0.03, 0.95, f"$p = {row['p_norm']:.3f}$",
                transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=FS_LEGEND*1.,
                va='top', ha='left',
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.4', fc='white',
                          ec='0.6', alpha=0.9))
        if i == 0:
            ax.legend(loc='lower right', fontsize=FS_LEGEND * 1., frameon=True)
        _label(ax)

    return fig

# Let's write a function to visualize the normative charts

def plot_charts(ax, dummy_ages, predicted_moments, query_index):
    # extract predicted moments
    y_ppc_mu_mean = predicted_moments['mu_estimate'][:, query_index]
    y_ppc_sigma_mean = predicted_moments['std_estimate'][:, query_index]

    quantiles = [0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.95, 0.99, 0.999]

    thickness_quantiles = {
        q: (
            (
                y_ppc_mu_mean + stats.norm.ppf(q=q) * (y_ppc_sigma_mean)
            )
        ) for q in quantiles
    }

    # colors for the plot
    c1 = '#448e9c'  # brighter shade
    c2 = '#038da6'  # darker shade

    # centile plots
    for q1, q2, alpha in [(0.001, 0.999, 0.05), (0.01, 0.99, 0.1), (0.05, 0.95, 0.2), (0.25, 0.75, 0.3)]:
        ax.fill_between(
            dummy_ages,
            thickness_quantiles[q1],
            thickness_quantiles[q2],
            alpha=alpha,
            color=c1,
        )

        # Now add boundary lines with different colors
        ax.plot(dummy_ages, thickness_quantiles[q1], color=c1, lw=0.5, linestyle=":",)
        ax.plot(dummy_ages, thickness_quantiles[q2], color=c1, lw=0.5, linestyle=":",)

    # Median
    ax.plot(
        dummy_ages,
        thickness_quantiles[0.5],
        c=c2,
        lw=4,
    )

    ax.set_xlim(3.5,96.5)
    
    ax.set_ylabel(f"Mode: {query_index + 1}")

class MyNumpyEncoder(json.JSONEncoder):
    def default(self, obj):
        if isinstance(obj, np.integer):
            return int(obj)
        elif isinstance(obj, np.floating):
            return float(obj)
        elif isinstance(obj, np.ndarray):
            return obj.tolist()

def ensure_dir(file_name):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(file_name), exist_ok=True)
    return file_name


def list_dirs(path=os.getcwd()):
    files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, '*'))
    files = [x for x in files if os.path.isdir(x)]
    return files


def file_exists(file_name, path_name=os.getcwd()):
    return os.path.isfile(os.path.join(path_name, file_name))

def plot_single_view_with_cerebro(
        dscalar_data, ax, colormap=plt.cm.coolwarm, clims=None, vlims=None, exclusion_color=(1.,1.,1.,0),
        view="L", show_colorbar=False, colorbar_format=None, cifti_left_right_seperation=0,
        surface = 'midthickness', spheres=None):
    try:
        
        my_brain_viewer = cbv.Cerebro_brain_viewer(offscreen=True, background_color=(1.,1.,1.,0), null_color=(1., 1., 1., 0.0), no_color=(0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 1.))

        surface_model = my_brain_viewer.load_template_GIFTI_cortical_surface_models(surface)

        cifti_space = my_brain_viewer.visualize_cifti_space(
            volumetric_structures='none', cifti_left_right_seperation=cifti_left_right_seperation,
        )

        dscalar_layer = my_brain_viewer.add_cifti_dscalar_layer(
            dscalar_data=dscalar_data,
            colormap=colormap,
            clims=clims,
            vlims=vlims,
            exclusion_color=exclusion_color,
            opacity=0.95)
        
        if spheres is not None:
            my_brain_viewer.visualize_spheres(
                coordinates=spheres[0] + (spheres[2] @ np.array([[cifti_left_right_seperation/2, 0, 0]])),
                radii=1*np.ones(spheres[0].shape),
                color=spheres[1],
            )

        ax.axis('off')
        camconf = my_brain_viewer._view_to_camera_config(view)

def plot_left_right_surface_with_cerebro(dscalar_data, fig, ax, colormap=plt.cm.coolwarm, clims=None, show_colorbar=False, spheres=None, colorbar_format=None, **kwargs):
    # Hide the parent axis
    ax.set_visible(False)

    # Create a 2x2 GridSpec within the axis using inset_axes
    gs = ax.inset_axes([0, 0, 1, 1], transform=ax.transAxes)
    sub_gs = GridSpec(2, 2, gs, hspace=0., wspace=0.)

    # Create a 4x4 grid
    ax_tl = fig.add_subplot(sub_gs[0, 0])
    ax_tr = fig.add_subplot(sub_gs[0, 1])
    ax_bl = fig.add_subplot(sub_gs[1, 0])
    ax_br = fig.add_subplot(sub_gs[1, 1])
    
    # separate data to left and right
    dscalar_data_left = dscalar_data.copy()
    dscalar_data_left[left_cortical_surface_model.index_count:] = np.nan
    dscalar_data_right = dscalar_data.copy()
    dscalar_data_right[:left_cortical_surface_model.index_count] = np.nan
    
    # separate spheres to left and right
    if spheres is None:
        left_spheres = None
        right_spheres = None
    else:
        left_spheres_mask = (spheres[2][:,0] == -1)
        left_spheres = [spheres[0][left_spheres_mask], spheres[1], spheres[2][left_spheres_mask]]
        right_spheres_mask = (spheres[2][:,0] == 1)
        right_spheres = [spheres[0][right_spheres_mask], spheres[1], spheres[2][right_spheres_mask]]
    
    # Lateral left view
    plot_single_view_with_cerebro(dscalar_data_left, ax_tl, colormap=colormap, clims=clims,
                                  view=((-420, 0, 0), None, None, None), spheres=left_spheres, **kwargs)
    # Medial left view
    plot_single_view_with_cerebro(dscalar_data_left, ax_bl, colormap=colormap, clims=clims,
                                  view=((420, 0, 0), None, None, None), spheres=left_spheres, cifti_left_right_seperation=-80, **kwargs)
    
    # Lateral right view
    plot_single_view_with_cerebro(dscalar_data_right, ax_tr, colormap=colormap, clims=clims,
                                  view=((420, 0, 0), None, None, None), spheres=right_spheres, **kwargs)
    # Medial right view
    plot_single_view_with_cerebro(dscalar_data_right, ax_br, colormap=colormap, clims=clims,
                                  view=((-420, 0, 0), None, None, None), spheres=right_spheres, cifti_left_right_seperation=-80, **kwargs)

    if show_colorbar:
        cax = inset_axes(
            ax,
            width="30%",
            height="4%",
            loc="center",
            bbox_to_anchor=(-0., 0.0, 1., 1.),
            bbox_transform=ax.transAxes,
            borderpad=0,
        )
        cb = fig.colorbar(
            mpl.cm.ScalarMappable(
                norm=mpl.colors.Normalize(vmin=clims[0], vmax=clims[1]),
                cmap=colormap
            ),
            cax=cax,
            aspect=10,
            orientation='horizontal',
            format=colorbar_format,
        )
        cb.outline.set_visible(False)

def compute_normative_trajectories_for_atlas(atlas_file, output_file, spectral_basis_predictions, lookup=False):
    atlas = nib.load(atlas_file)

    atlas_label_dict = dict(list(atlas.header.get_index_map(0).named_maps)[0].label_table)
    atlas_label_names = {i:atlas_label_dict[i].label for i in atlas_label_dict}
    atlas_label_indices = {atlas_label_dict[i].label:i for i in atlas_label_dict}
    if lookup:
        atlas_data = atlas.get_fdata()[0][surface_mask]
    else:
        atlas_data = atlas.get_fdata()[0][:snm_1000.eigenmode_basis.eigenvectors.shape[0]]

    atlas_queries = {}
    # loop over cortical labels
    for label_index in np.unique(atlas_data):
        if label_index != 0:
            label_name = atlas_label_names[label_index]
            # mean thickness over region
            signal = average_operator(atlas_data == label_index)
            atlas_queries[f'{label_name}'] = signal
    
    atlas_query_names = [x for x in atlas_queries]
    atlas_queries_matrix = np.array([atlas_queries[x] for x in atlas_query_names]).T

    encoded_normative_queries = snm_1000.eigenmode_basis.encode(atlas_queries_matrix.T, n_modes=1000)

    # predict moments
    predicted_moments = snm_1000.predict(
        encoded_query=encoded_normative_queries.T,
        spectral_predictions=spectral_basis_predictions,
        n_modes=1000,
    ).predictions

    # create a dataframe to hold results
    # each row is an age, each column is a region, (two parent columns for mu and sigma)
    predicted_moments_df = pd.DataFrame(
        data=np.concatenate([predicted_moments['mu_estimate'], predicted_moments['std_estimate']], axis=1),
        index=candidate_ages,
        columns=pd.MultiIndex.from_product([['Mean (mm)', 'SD (mm)'], atlas_query_names])
    )
    predicted_moments_df.index.name = 'Age (years)'

    # save to csv
    predicted_moments_df.to_csv(output_file)

    return predicted_moments_df

class MyNumpyEncoder(json.JSONEncoder):
    def default(self, obj):
        if isinstance(obj, np.integer):
            return int(obj)
        elif isinstance(obj, np.floating):
            return float(obj)
        elif isinstance(obj, np.ndarray):
            return obj.tolist()
        else:
            return super(MyEncoder, self).default(obj)


def ensure_dir(file_name):

    return file_name

    files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, '*'))
    files = [x for x in files if os.path.isdir(x)]
    return files

def show_image(image_path, width=1000, resample=PILImage.LANCZOS):
    """
    Display an image in Jupyter at a fixed width while preserving aspect ratio.
    The image is resampled (not embedded full-size) to reduce notebook memory.
    """
    img = PILImage.open(image_path).copy()
    w, h = img.size
    new_h = int(h * width / w)
    img = img.resize((width, new_h), resample)
    display(img)

dscalar = nib.load(dscalar_file)

# extract surface information
lx, ly, lz = left_surface.darrays[0].data.T
lt = left_surface.darrays[1].data
rx, ry, rz = right_surface.darrays[0].data.T
rt = right_surface.darrays[1].data

# combine into a complete brain
lrx = np.concatenate([lx - expand, rx + expand])
lry = np.concatenate([ly, ry])
lrz = np.concatenate([lz, rz])
lrt = np.concatenate([lt, (rt + lx.shape[0])])

lxyz = left_surface.darrays[0].data
rxyz = right_surface.darrays[0].data
lrxyz = np.array([lrx, lry, lrz]).T

# create a mapping between surface and cifti vertices

surface_to_cifti = {}

def plot_single_view_with_cerebro(
        dscalar_data, ax, colormap=plt.cm.coolwarm, clims=None, vlims=None, exclusion_color=(1.,1.,1.,0),
        view="L", show_colorbar=False, colorbar_format=None, cifti_left_right_seperation=0,
        surface = 'midthickness', spheres=None):
    try:
        
        my_brain_viewer = cbv.Cerebro_brain_viewer(offscreen=True, background_color=(1.,1.,1.,0), null_color=(1., 1., 1., 0.0), no_color=(0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 1.))

        surface_model = my_brain_viewer.load_template_GIFTI_cortical_surface_models(surface)

        cifti_space = my_brain_viewer.visualize_cifti_space(
            volumetric_structures='none', cifti_left_right_seperation=cifti_left_right_seperation,
        )

        dscalar_layer = my_brain_viewer.add_cifti_dscalar_layer(
            dscalar_data=dscalar_data,
            colormap=colormap,
            clims=clims,
            vlims=vlims,
            exclusion_color=exclusion_color,
            opacity=0.95)
        
        if spheres is not None:
            my_brain_viewer.visualize_spheres(
                coordinates=spheres[0] + (spheres[2] @ np.array([[cifti_left_right_seperation/2, 0, 0]])),
                radii=1*np.ones(spheres[0].shape),
                color=spheres[1],
            )

        ax.axis('off')
        camconf = my_brain_viewer._view_to_camera_config(view)
        # camconf = my_brain_viewer.zoom_camera_to_content(camconf)
        my_brain_viewer.viewer.change_view(**camconf)
        my_brain_viewer.offscreen_draw_to_matplotlib_axes(ax)

    finally:
        my_brain_viewer.viewer.window.destroy()

def plot_left_right_surface_with_cerebro(dscalar_data, fig, ax, colormap=plt.cm.coolwarm, clims=None, show_colorbar=False, spheres=None, colorbar_format=None, **kwargs):
    # Hide the parent axis
    ax.set_visible(False)

    # Create a 2x2 GridSpec within the axis using inset_axes
    gs = ax.inset_axes([0, 0, 1, 1], transform=ax.transAxes)
    sub_gs = GridSpec(2, 2, gs, hspace=0., wspace=0.)

    # Create a 4x4 grid
    ax_tl = fig.add_subplot(sub_gs[0, 0])
    ax_tr = fig.add_subplot(sub_gs[0, 1])
    ax_bl = fig.add_subplot(sub_gs[1, 0])
    ax_br = fig.add_subplot(sub_gs[1, 1])
    
    # separate data to left and right
    dscalar_data_left = dscalar_data.copy()
    dscalar_data_left[left_cortical_surface_model.index_count:] = np.nan
    dscalar_data_right = dscalar_data.copy()
    dscalar_data_right[:left_cortical_surface_model.index_count] = np.nan
    
    # separate spheres to left and right
    if spheres is None:
        left_spheres = None
        right_spheres = None
    else:
        left_spheres_mask = (spheres[2][:,0] == -1)
        left_spheres = [spheres[0][left_spheres_mask], spheres[1], spheres[2][left_spheres_mask]]
        right_spheres_mask = (spheres[2][:,0] == 1)
        right_spheres = [spheres[0][right_spheres_mask], spheres[1], spheres[2][right_spheres_mask]]
    
    # Lateral left view
    plot_single_view_with_cerebro(dscalar_data_left, ax_tl, colormap=colormap, clims=clims,
                                  view=((-420, 0, 0), None, None, None), spheres=left_spheres, **kwargs)
    # Medial left view
    plot_single_view_with_cerebro(dscalar_data_left, ax_bl, colormap=colormap, clims=clims,
                                  view=((420, 0, 0), None, None, None), spheres=left_spheres, cifti_left_right_seperation=-80, **kwargs)
    
    # Lateral right view
    plot_single_view_with_cerebro(dscalar_data_right, ax_tr, colormap=colormap, clims=clims,
                                  view=((420, 0, 0), None, None, None), spheres=right_spheres, **kwargs)
    # Medial right view
    plot_single_view_with_cerebro(dscalar_data_right, ax_br, colormap=colormap, clims=clims,
                                  view=((-420, 0, 0), None, None, None), spheres=right_spheres, cifti_left_right_seperation=-80, **kwargs)

    if show_colorbar:
        cax = inset_axes(
            ax,
            width="30%",
            height="4%",
            loc="center",
            bbox_to_anchor=(-0., 0.0, 1., 1.),
            bbox_transform=ax.transAxes,
            borderpad=0,
        )
        cb = fig.colorbar(
            mpl.cm.ScalarMappable(
                norm=mpl.colors.Normalize(vmin=clims[0], vmax=clims[1]),
                cmap=colormap
            ),
            cax=cax,
            aspect=10,
            orientation='horizontal',
            format=colorbar_format,
        )
        cb.outline.set_visible(False)
        cb.ax.tick_params(labelsize=12)
        cb.ax.tick_params(length=0)

        if isinstance(obj, np.integer):
            return int(obj)
        elif isinstance(obj, np.floating):
            return float(obj)
        elif isinstance(obj, np.ndarray):

    files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, '*'))

def plot_data_on_brain_surface(data, title="", cmap=mycm, symmetric_cbar=True, vmax=None, vmin=None, background_data=sulcal_depth.get_fdata()[0], darkness=0.1, auto_vlim_quantile=0.05, colorbar_format=None):
    """
    Plot a cifti-like data over the fs-LR32k surface space.
    ----------------------------------------------------------------
    Parameters:
        - data: a vector of shape (59412,) to be visualized.
        - title: the title of generated plot.
        - cmap: the colormap used for the plot.
        - symmetric_cbar: bool, Specifies whether the 
          colorbar should be symmetric (centered at zero).
        - vmax: colorbar max limit.
        - vmin: colorbar min limit.
        - background data: a surface data to project as a shadow
          behind the main data. (use None for no background)
        - darkness: the background effect
        - auto_vlim_quantile: the quantile to define vmin and vmax
          automatically (should be in the range of [0,0.5)]).
        - colorbar_format: string format for numbers in colorbar.
    ----------------------------------------------------------------
    """
    # Initialization
    if vmax is None:
        vmax = np.quantile(data,1 - auto_vlim_quantile)
    if vmin is None:
        vmin = np.quantile(data,auto_vlim_quantile)
    if symmetric_cbar:
        (vmin, vmax) = -max(abs(vmin), abs(vmax)), max(abs(vmin), abs(vmax))
    if background_data is not None:
        background = True
    else:
        background = False
    
    # surface center
    cxyz=(lrxyz.min(0) + lrxyz.max(0))/2

    # transfer data to surface scalar
    surface_scalars = np.empty(lrx.shape[0])
    surface_scalars[:] = np.nan
    surface_scalars[surface_mask] = data.copy()

    # decompose left and right information
    left_surface_scalars = surface_scalars[:lx.shape[0]]
    right_surface_scalars = surface_scalars[-rx.shape[0]:]
    
    # Generate background data
    surface_background_data = np.zeros(lrx.shape[0])
    surface_background_data[surface_mask] = background_data.copy()
    left_background_data = surface_background_data[:lx.shape[0]]
    right_background_data = surface_background_data[-rx.shape[0]:]


    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(8, 8), subplot_kw={'projection': '3d'});

    zoom_coeff = 0.85

    # 'lateral', 'medial', 'dorsal', 'ventral', 'anterior', 'posterior'
    plotting.plot_surf(
        [lxyz-cxyz, lt],
        left_surface_scalars,
        axes=axes[0,0],
        view='lateral',
        colorbar=False,
        symmetric_cbar=False,
        darkness=darkness,
        vmax=vmax,
        vmin=vmin,
        cmap=cmap,
        bg_on_data=background,
        bg_map=left_background_data,
    );
    axes[0,0].set_xlim3d(np.array(axes[0,0].get_xlim3d())*zoom_coeff)
    axes[0,0].set_ylim3d(np.array(axes[0,0].get_ylim3d())*zoom_coeff)
    axes[0,0].set_zlim3d(np.array(axes[0,0].get_zlim3d())*zoom_coeff)

    plotting.plot_surf(
        [rxyz-cxyz, rt],
        right_surface_scalars,
        axes=axes[0,1],
        view='medial',
        colorbar=False,
        symmetric_cbar=False,
        darkness=darkness,
        vmax=vmax,
        vmin=vmin,
        cmap=cmap,
        bg_on_data=background,
        bg_map=right_background_data,
    );
    axes[0,1].set_xlim3d(np.array(axes[0,1].get_xlim3d())*zoom_coeff)
    axes[0,1].set_ylim3d(np.array(axes[0,1].get_ylim3d())*zoom_coeff)
    axes[0,1].set_zlim3d(np.array(axes[0,1].get_zlim3d())*zoom_coeff)


    plotting.plot_surf(
        [lxyz-cxyz, lt],
        left_surface_scalars,
        axes=axes[1,0],
        view='medial',
        colorbar=False,
        symmetric_cbar=False,
        darkness=darkness,
        vmax=vmax,
        vmin=vmin,
        cmap=cmap,
        bg_on_data=background,
        bg_map=left_background_data,
    );
    axes[1,0].set_xlim3d(np.array(axes[1,0].get_xlim3d())*zoom_coeff)
    axes[1,0].set_ylim3d(np.array(axes[1,0].get_ylim3d())*zoom_coeff)
    axes[1,0].set_zlim3d(np.array(axes[1,0].get_zlim3d())*zoom_coeff)

    plotting.plot_surf(
        [rxyz-cxyz, rt],
        right_surface_scalars,
        axes=axes[1,1],
        view='lateral',
        colorbar=False,
        symmetric_cbar=False,
        darkness=darkness,
        vmax=vmax,
        vmin=vmin,
        cmap=cmap,
        bg_on_data=background,
        bg_map=right_background_data,
    );
    axes[1,1].set_xlim3d(np.array(axes[1,1].get_xlim3d())*zoom_coeff)
    axes[1,1].set_ylim3d(np.array(axes[1,1].get_ylim3d())*zoom_coeff)
    axes[1,1].set_zlim3d(np.array(axes[1,1].get_zlim3d())*zoom_coeff)

    fig.suptitle(title, fontsize=24, y=0.98);
    plt.subplots_adjust(left=0, bottom=0, right=1, top=1, wspace=-0., hspace=-0.25)

    from mpl_toolkits.axes_grid1.inset_locator import inset_axes
    axins = inset_axes(
        axes[0,0],
        width="30%",
        height="4%",
        loc="center",
        bbox_to_anchor=(-0., 0.02, 1., 1.),
        bbox_transform=fig.transFigure,
        borderpad=0,
    )
    cb = fig.colorbar(
        mpl.cm.ScalarMappable(
            norm=mpl.colors.Normalize(vmin=vmin, vmax=vmax),
            cmap=cmap
        ),
        cax=axins,
        aspect=10,
        orientation='horizontal',
        format=colorbar_format,
    )
    cb.outline.set_visible(False)
    cb.ax.tick_params(labelsize=12)
    cb.ax.tick_params(length=0)

docs.text: Using the normative models fitted in chapter 6, we now turn our attention to generating exemplary interactive visualizations to better showcase the findings.

docs.title: Create a fixed BSpline function to ensure consistent nonlinear expansions of age across all models¶
Load selected covariance pairs¶
docs.text: The largest pairs of kernels in terms of correlation are stored to model a sparse covariance structure.

docs.title: Also Load observed training moments (mean and sigma used for standardization)¶
Data preparations¶
docs.text: Here we'll prepare the data that will be used in the visualizations

docs.text: Here we'll write the functions to generate the visualizations
